Section 122 imposes a statutory period of limitation for court-martial trials subject to exceptions and accrual rules. Rule 27 contains delay-report safeguards. The legally relevant timeline cannot be inferred from incident date alone, nor can a delay be cured by informal action.
Build chronology: act/omission, discovery of offence, knowledge of perpetrator, action dates, status changes.; Assess Section 122(1)-(3), exceptions and exclusions with JAG.; Use prescribed delay reports where required.; Keep litigation holds and explain any delays factually.
Assuming universal three-year period from incident; Ignoring knowledge-based starting points or exceptions; Fudging dates

title: Procedural suspension: Army Rule 36
body:
Rule 36 permits specified procedural rules, including Rules 23, 24, 33, 34 and Rule 95(2), to be suspended by empowered officers where statutory military exigencies or disciplinary necessity render compliance impossible or inexpedient. It is not a generic permission to dispense with Rule 22 or Rule 26.
Verify that the official competent authority, conditions and target rule match Rule 36.; Insist on an order under the authority’s hand specifying the exigency or necessity.; Assess actual geographical/operational factual context with JAG.; Retain direction and limit deviation strictly to authorised scope.
Using Rule 36 as standard shortcut; Purporting to suspend Rule 22; Undocumented emergency

title: Accused rights before trial: Rules 33–34
body:
Before trial, the Rules prescribe rights to prepare defence and warning requirements. These are different from the earlier Rule 22/23 participatory rights. Exact timelines and documents depend on the mode of trial and applicable exceptions.
Determine trial type and current applicable rules.; Ensure specified access to charge, evidence and assistance before trial.; Calculate notice period on actual service dates and applicable exceptions.; Retain proof of delivery and any waiver recognised by law.
Importing Rule 26 24-hour standard into every court-martial; Ignoring trial-specific rights

title: Court of Inquiry to Rule 22/23 transition
body:
CoI, hearing of charge and SoE are separate processes. A CoI report may identify questions for disciplinary decision-making, but the correct Rule 22 proviso or fresh hearing route must be selected lawfully; CoI witness material is not automatically sworn trial evidence.
Review CoI scope, affected-person rights and evidence restrictions.; Determine whether Rule 22 proviso is actually available.; Frame an allegation supported by admissible facts.; Order SoE, if appropriate, and give the accused relevant rights.
Using CoI recommendation as finding of guilt; Ignoring Rule 182; Silently duplicating/wasting witness process

title: Civil-offence intersection and new criminal codes
body:
Military handling of a civil offence requires attention to Section 69, jurisdictional exceptions under Section 70 and court-choice provisions. India’s post-2024 criminal-law framework requires careful offence-date and substitution checking; a generic legacy IPC reference is not sufficient for every new case.
Identify incident and offence dates, territory and civilian nexus.; Map the actual criminal law in force on the material date and the Army Act charging route.; Evaluate jurisdiction and coordination with police/ordinary criminal court.; Check Section 120(2) before SCM consideration.
Mixing IPC/BNS labels mechanically; Assuming sole military jurisdiction; Using an obsolete charge pro forma

title: Quality assurance of charge documentation
body:
A reproducible legal record should identify the allegation, statutory basis, accused status, procedural opportunities, authorised route and actual evidence. Local checklists supplement but never replace current prescribed forms.
Maintain single case ID and unaltered event chronology.; Use role-appropriate authorised forms; distinguish charge, witness evidence and decisions.; Reference page/annexure numbers and log corrections.; Perform pre-signature legal and administrative checklist verification.
Inconsistent names/dates; Missing witness signatures; Unsigned decision; Draft forms presented as statutory

title: How to read the judgment and apply precedent
body:
A case digest should identify the fact pattern, legal question, holding, limitation and subsequent treatment. Virendra Kumar addresses Rule 180 defects and their timing; P S Gill addresses AFT power over a convening order and scrutiny of prima-facie charges. Neither is a standing blanket immunity or blanket automatic invalidity rule.
Locate exact official judgment and paragraph.; Write the fact-specific holding in own words.; Identify whether the case concerns pretrial review, trial outcome or jurisdiction.; Search subsequent binding treatment before operational reliance.
Quote-mining dicta; Treating any defect as always fatal; Claiming precedents have not changed without checking
references: [SC_PPS: military pretrial safeguards discussion]; [SC_VK: paras 9-13]; [SC_GILL: paras 11-18]

title: Role-separation, escalation and non-automation
body:
The eventual application provides information, factual checks and draft reference. It cannot constitute a court, issue a punishment, settle contested facts or exercise command discretion. High-risk decisions must remain under a competent commander with JAG advice.
Require case user to select rank, offence date, current command authority and requested outcome.; Show source, version, unresolved facts and alternative legal routes.; Block automatic generation of definitive punishment orders in uncleared cases.; Capture JAG review, change history and audit evidence.
Uncited legal conclusions; Auto-populated rank/authority without verification; Overconfident advice from incomplete law

title: Soldier denies an alleged verbal order
body:
A section commander alleges disobedience; the soldier says the order was neither lawful nor communicated.
Record exact alleged order, time, witnesses and supporting duty documents.; Conduct a genuine Rule 22 hearing with adverse testimony and defence opportunity.; Test whether statutory offence elements are disclosed; consider Rule 22(2).; Select permitted Rule 22(3) route only if legally warranted.
Discipline cannot substitute for proof of the actual instruction.
references: AR r22(1)-(3); AA relevant offence section

title: Rule 180 not complied with during prior CoI
body:
An officer was adversely named in a CoI and not allowed to cross-examine witnesses.
Retrieve CoI and Rule 180 record.; Do not assume Rule 22(1) can be dispensed with.; Assess fresh hearing and corrective action; consult JAG.
CoI non-compliance is neither automatically harmless nor automatically fatal to every later trial.
references: AR r22(1) proviso and r180; Virendra Kumar paras 11-13

title: Defence witness is not recorded in SoE
body:
An eyewitness supporting the accused was named but omitted from the Summary of Evidence.
Verify relevance and tender; document omission.; Arrange lawful completion/correction while witness remains available.; Reassess Rule 24 decision after a complete record.
An SoE is not meant to be a prosecution-only file.

title: NCO awarded confinement to lines
body:
A commander proposes seven days confinement to lines for a Havildar.
Identify NCO status at offence and award.; Check express Section 81(4) prohibition concerning Section 80(a)-(c).; Do not use the prohibited punishment; refer to competent authorised alternatives.
A short duration does not make a rank-prohibited punishment lawful.

title: Sepoy proposed for severe reprimand
body:
The CO considers severe reprimand of a sepoy.
Verify rank and Section 81(5).; Reject Section 80(g) for below NCO.; Consider lawful route, with independent safeguards.
Punishment types are rank-dependent.

title: JCO to be reprimanded by Lt Col CO
body:
A Lt Col CO considers severe reprimand under Section 85.
Check Section 85 CO rank restriction.; Confirm actual legally competent authority.; Do not award in conflict with the Colonel-rank proviso.
Not all CO rank appointments carry identical summary powers.

title: Captain referred for superior summary disposal
body:
An officer below field-officer rank faces a charge and is to be dealt with under Section 83.
Check actual Section 83 competence.; Serve charge and SoE at least 24 hours before disposal under Rule 26(1).; Hear witnesses unless written consent validly dispenses with attendance; forward record.
Receipt of a charge is not consent to omit evidence.

title: Major faces loss of seniority proposal
body:
Superior authority contemplates Section 84(a) punishment.
Verify eligibility and superior statutory authority.; Document accused’s right to elect trial by court-martial before award.; Ensure Rule 26 compliance and review route.
Missing an election opportunity is a serious statutory issue.

title: Civil theft case proposed for SCM
body:
Soldier faces alleged theft from a civilian shop under Section 69.
Check applicable civil law and Army Act offence.; Review Section 70 and Section 120(2) restrictions.; Refer to authorised superior unless legally established exception applies.
SCM is not the default for a civil offence.

title: Witness abroad: signed statement supplied
body:
Critical witness sends an emailed signed statement but cannot attend SoE.
Verify genuineness and actual availability.; Have recording officer consider certification under Rule 23(5).; Read statement to accused and record rights; alert trial authority of cross-examination issue.
Convenience alone is not a substitute for statutory grounds.

title: New allegation appears during SoE
body:
Original charge concerns lateness; witness now alleges forged movement entry.
Distinguish new allegation and evidence.; Review Rule 22(4) and proper charge framing.; Provide applicable procedural safeguards for revised allegations; seek JAG.
Do not punish for an undisclosed new charge.

title: Rule 36 claimed due to operational urgency
body:
Commander wants to skip Rule 22 hearing during exercise.
Check exact Rule 36 text and eligible provisions.; Rule 22 is not listed among rules suspendable by Rule 36 in consulted text.; Stop unsupported waiver; refer through proper authority.
Operational pressure is not automatic legal authorisation.

title: Retired officer and continuing proceedings
body:
An officer retires while disciplinary allegations are being processed.
Identify offence and retirement dates and status under Section 123.; Assess Section 122 limitation and authority with JAG.; Check controlling precedents including P S Gill on facts and jurisdiction.
Retirement does not by itself answer all jurisdiction questions.

title: SoE shows charge cannot be substantiated
body:
Witnesses retract allegation, and documents exculpate accused.
CO considers complete record under Rule 24.; Assess re-hearing and dismissal route under Rule 24(1)(c).; Document decision and preservation requirements.
Recording SoE does not predetermine trial.

title: Punishment award to be reviewed
body:
Superior requests file after summary award against JCO.
Find Sections 86-88 and Rule 26(3).; Forward prescribed authenticated documents through proper channel.; Record any subsequent legal review action.
Summary award is not exempt from statutory scrutiny.

title: Lt Col Prithi Pal Singh Bedi v Union of India
body:
Rule 22-24 stages are antecedent to trial and must be analysed with the complete court-martial process; not every preliminary defect equals trial conviction invalidity.
Complex multi-petitioner decision; consult precise passage and intervening law.
references: SC_PPS Judgment discussion of rr 22-25, pretrial rights, constitutional argument

title: Union of India v Ex Sep Virendra Kumar
body:
Rule 180 procedural safeguards must be honoured; timely objection at charge/SoE stages calls for rectification; trial consequences turn on full procedural context and findings.
Do not read as dispensing with mandatory Rule 180 process.

title: Union of India v P S Gill
body:
AFT jurisdiction can reach a service matter concerning the convening of a GCM; prima-facie basis for charges may be scrutinised in the particular procedural posture.
Not general licence to ask a tribunal to substitute merits decision for any pending inquiry; check facts and subsequent case law.

title: Purpose and scope of Volume IV
body: A court-martial is a legally constituted trial forum distinct from a Court of Inquiry, charge hearing and summary punishment. The lawful forum depends on personal jurisdiction, offence, rank, command, warrant or other authority, date and statutory limits. Record accused service status at relevant dates, present status and effective attachment. Identify every alleged act/omission and Army Act offence, considering civil-offence jurisdiction. Check trial forum, convening competence and any applicable warrants/restrictions. Preserve earlier CoI, Rule 22, SoE and service records without treating those steps as a conviction. AA §§2, 108–127; AR rr33–36; AFT §15

title: The four kinds of courts-martial
body: Section 108 recognises GCM, DCM, SGCM and SCM. A label alone supplies no authority: each has separate convening, composition, jurisdiction and sentencing constraints. Identify potential type, then test rank and offence jurisdiction. Match to the correct statutory constituting/convening provision. Check sentencing ceiling and pretrial rule set. Record why the selected type is lawful. AA §108(a)–(d)

title: Who may convene a GCM or DCM
body: GCM may be convened by the Central Government, COAS or an officer empowered by COAS warrant. DCM may be convened by a GCM-convening officer or an officer empowered by warrant of such officer. Actual warrant limitations matter. Locate the operative signed warrant or statutory authority. Check rank, geographical reach, conditions/reservations and effective date. Apply Rule 37 pre-convening evaluation to the material. Retain warrant and signed convening order within the court record. AA §§109–111; AR r37

title: SGCM: legally confined convening grounds
body: SGCM may be convened by specifically empowered officers, specified officers on active service or the commander of a detached force on active service in the limited statutory circumstances. The name does not imply an unrestricted shortcut. Identify the exact paragraph of Section 112 relied on. Establish active-service and/or statutory power facts if material. Document why the GCM route is impracticable when invoking clause (c). Verify the minimum composition and other applicable rules. AA §112(a)–(c); AA §115

title: SCM constitution and attendees
body: A qualifying commanding officer alone constitutes an SCM. Two other officers/JCOs, or one of either, attend throughout; their role differs fundamentally from voting members of GCM/DCM/SGCM. Check legal CO and command of accused. Identify two qualified attendees and document uninterrupted attendance. Follow the separate SCM trial rules and record requirements. Do not treat attendees as sworn court members. AA §116(1)–(2); AR rr106–109

title: GCM, DCM and SGCM composition: statutory minima
body: GCM requires at least five officers: each commissioned for at least three whole years and at least four not below captain. DCM requires at least three officers each commissioned at least two whole years. SGCM requires at least three officers. Further disqualifications and rank rules apply. Check commission dates and substantive/acting ranks with authorised records. Screen individual disqualifications under Rule 39. Apply Rule 40 requirements where relevant. Verify minimum strength through proceedings and any dissolution trigger. AA §§113–115; AR rr39–41

title: DCM limits and special warrant-officer protection
body: DCM may not try an officer or JCO. It cannot impose death, transportation or imprisonment exceeding two years. The express proviso prevents DCM from sentencing a warrant officer to imprisonment. Confirm accused rank and date-sensitive status. Verify whether DCM jurisdiction covers the alleged offence. Screen proposed punishments and the warrant-officer proviso. Escalate if any sentence beyond the forum ceiling is contemplated. AA §119

title: SCM personal jurisdiction and sentence limits
body: SCM can try persons subject to the Army Act and under command of the officer holding the court, but excludes officers, JCOs and warrant officers. No death or transportation; imprisonment maxima depend on rank of the officer holding SCM: one year if Lt Col or above, three months if below. Establish both Army Act status and command of trial officer. Exclude officer/JCO/WO categories expressly. Check trial officer rank and consequent imprisonment ceiling. Consider additional Section 120(2) restriction separately. AA §120(1),(3)–(5)

title: Restricted SCM offences and reference to higher authority
body: For offences under AA §§34, 37, 69 or against the officer holding SCM, the statutory condition concerning grave reasons for immediate action and reference to a competent officer must be addressed. The cases stress the significance of these safeguards and recording the legal basis. Identify whether the alleged offence falls within the enumerated category. Consider factual grounds for urgency and whether reference can occur without detriment to discipline. Where reference is required, transmit the file to the specified competent authority. If exceptional non-reference is relied on, preserve actual reasons and AR r130 explanatory record. AA §120(2); AR r130; Vishav Priya Singh ¶¶20–23; Randhir Singh ¶¶9–14
references: AA §120(2); AR r130; Vishav Priya Singh ¶¶20–23; Randhir Singh ¶¶9–14

title: SCM and attached-unit Commanding Officer
body: The Supreme Court recognises particular circumstances in which the CO of a unit to which a person is properly attached can constitute the SCM. A factual attachment and legal command analysis is essential; parent-unit designation alone does not decide every case. Collect complete attachment orders with effective dates. Map incident location, date, actual unit of command and which CO had seisin. Apply the Supreme Court categories to facts without extrapolation. Refer any dual-command situation to JAG before trial. AA §§116,120(3); Vishav Priya Singh ¶¶24 onwards

title: Limitation to commence trial
body: The normal limitation is three years, subject to rules on commencement tied to date of offence, knowledge or known identity; statutory exceptions cover desertion, fraudulent enrolment and Section 37 offences, and particular periods are excluded. The date trial commences is a legal question. Prepare chronology: offence, discovery, identity discovery, action and contemplated trial commencement. Apply the earliest relevant knowledge rule in Section 122(1). Test Section 122(2) exceptions and (3)/(4) qualifications separately. Have JAG independently verify computation; do not assume a CoI or SoE pauses limitation. AA §122(1)–(4)

title: Trial after discharge, retirement or ceasing subject to Act
body: Section 123 permits trial in defined circumstances after a person ceases to be subject to the Act, but contains a separate three-year post-cessation timing requirement, exclusions and exceptions. Its operation must be considered alongside Section 122. Confirm status at offence, cessation date and current location. Calculate both Section 122 and Section 123 timelines, including permitted exclusions. Identify statutory exceptions without making general assumptions. Obtain specialised JAG review before any military custody or trial decision. AA §123(1)–(4); §122

title: Civil court versus court-martial and omitted Section 127
body: Where both courts have jurisdiction, Sections 125–126 allocate decision and dispute procedures to specified authorities. Section 127 on successive trials was omitted in 1992, so older books describing it as live law are unsafe. Identify civilian-law offence and applicable Section 69 conditions. Identify competent Section 125 authority and any formal criminal court notice. Document consultation and decision on forum under Sections 125–126. Flag any prior trial/sanction and Section 121 prohibition. AA §§69,70,125,126; AA §127 [omitted 1992]

title: Rule 37: convening officer must examine the case
body: For GCM/DCM the convening officer must first be satisfied that the charges disclose Army Act offences and that the evidence justifies trial; an insufficient case must not simply be passed on for the trial court to sort out. Review charge wording and exact elements. Match each charge to SoE/abstract evidence and defence material. Verify cognisance and competence, including limitation. Record actual pre-convening review and issue appropriate order. AR r37(1)–(4); AA §§109–111

title: Ineligible members, bias and independent court
body: Rule 39 addresses ineligibility/disqualification, while Rule 40 imposes composition requirements for GCM and rank considerations for trial of officers. Personal interest, prior participation and corps/department composition require careful legal assessment. Screen each prospective member against Rule 39. Map rank, corps/department and previous involvement. Record the convening officer’s legally relevant Rule 40 opinion/exceptions. Ensure accused can exercise statutory objections at trial. AR rr39–40; AA §§113–115,130; Prithi Pal Singh Bedi
references: AR rr39–40; AA §§113–115,130; Prithi Pal Singh Bedi

title: Court assembly, legality inquiry and objection
body: Court legality and competence are checked on assembly, followed by the accused’s opportunity to object to members under Section 130. The objection and response must be heard and recorded; challenges are not ceremonial. Lay convening order, charge-sheet and SoE before the court as required. Check constitution and jurisdiction before trial merits. Read member names and invite challenges in statutory sequence. Resolve, record and if needed replace challenged member lawfully. AA §130; AR rr41–44

title: Court dissolution and loss of minimum membership
body: A court reduced below legal minimum after commencement must be dissolved. Illness of accused or judge advocate can trigger dissolution where continuation is impossible; the statute addresses re-trial after dissolution. Record date the trial lawfully commenced. Monitor membership and continuity throughout. If minimum falls, apply Section 117 rather than improvising a replacement mid-trial. Seek JAG guidance on effect, orders and a possible fresh trial. AA §117; AR r38

title: Accused preparation and disclosure
body: The Rules contain specific requirements concerning defence preparation and warning of trial. Defence access to relevant documents, means to consult counsel/defending officer and realistic time are legal protections, subject only to specific authorised exceptions. Serve and record all material legally required for the chosen forum. Verify rule-specific notice/warning period from current authenticated text. Facilitate lawful consultation and defence-witness preparation. Record any legally permitted exception and opportunity for remedy. AR rr33–34; r95; rr96–101

title: Counsel, defending officer and friend of accused
body: For GCM/DCM the rules distinguish representing defending officers, assisting friends, and counsel; the friend has a different procedural role. SCM has its own rule about assistance. Do not promise identical rights in all forums. Ask accused about legally available assistance and document choice. Check counsel entitlement, permissions and any restriction for precise forum. Avoid conflict of interest in nominated officers. Document ability to confer and present defence under applicable rules. AR rr95–101; AR r129 (SCM friend)

title: Charge-sheet precision and amendment
body: Charge-sheet format, particulars and objections matter. A change in a charge or substitution of an offence cannot defeat safeguards or exceed competence merely because it appears administratively convenient. Map each allegation to statutory ingredients, dates, place, accused and evidence. Apply the correct charge-sheet rule and identify duplicative/alternative charges. Record objections and any lawful amendment and defence opportunities. Reassess forum, limitation and preparation if the case changes materially. AR rr28–32; r35; rr46–49

title: Military exigencies and narrow rule suspension
body: Rule 36 provides a conditional, written declaration procedure concerning specified rules under military exigencies or necessities of discipline; it does not authorise a blanket disregard of fair-trial requirements. Identify precisely which enumerated procedural rule is affected. Require contemporaneous lawful declaration by competent authority setting out circumstances. Preserve all practicable defence opportunity as rule requires. Seek JAG review; never infer a waiver just because an operation is ongoing. AR r36

title: Judge advocate at GCM and other courts
body: Every GCM must be attended by a judge advocate as prescribed. A DCM or SGCM may be attended by one. The statutory role of the judge advocate differs from the convening authority and members deciding findings. Determine mandatory/advisable appointment for chosen court. Verify proper JAG officer or approved substitute. Record all legally required presence and advice. Preserve procedural objections in proceedings. AA §129; AR procedural provisions

title: Plea of guilty safeguards at GCM/DCM
body: A plea of guilty is not a mere checkbox. Rule 52 requires explanation of nature/effect and special treatment for serious charges, while Rule 54 addresses the subsequent procedure. If defence material reveals misunderstanding, the plea must be reconsidered. Check accused understands language and ingredients of charge. Explain and record effect and consequences of guilty plea in legally prescribed manner. Examine whether record, SoE or statement is inconsistent with an unqualified guilty plea. Follow rule-based proof/mitigation and correct plea if indicated. AR rr51–55, esp r52(2),r54

title: Plea of not guilty, prosecution and defence evidence
body: The trial proceeds with oral/documentary evidence, legally administered oaths, examination and cross-examination under the applicable procedural and evidence rules. A pre-trial SoE is not automatically equivalent to a witness being tested at trial. Confirm plea and record sequence. Lead admissible prosecution evidence and allow appropriate cross-examination. Consider defence evidence and lawful objections. Identify missing material evidence, contradictions and admissibility issues explicitly. AR rr56–64; AA §§131,133,135

title: Evidence law and 2023 criminal-law transition
body: The 2025 Army Act text still expressly names the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 in Section 133. India’s replacement evidence statute creates an important transition/savings question that cannot be resolved by silent auto-substitution in an AI assistant. Inspect authenticated up-to-date Section 133 and BSA repeal/savings/amendment provisions. Identify proceedings dates and commencement events. Request formal JAG view on applicable evidence law in specific trial. Version the system’s rules rather than overwriting older historical applicability. AA §133 (2025 text); Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023

title: Electronic evidence: provenance and chain of custody
body: Digital records such as CCTV clips, device logs, emails and sensor data require independent proof of authenticity, custody and admissibility. The database should record evidentiary steps as best practice, not invent new statutory certification rules. Create original acquisition manifest and identify device/controller. Preserve original exports, timestamps, hashes, access history and chain-of-custody records. Obtain competent technical witness and applicable certification/legal foundation. Document transformations, redactions and derivative viewing copies. AA §133; applicable evidence law [VERIFY]; AR witness/exhibit procedure
references: AA §133; applicable evidence law [VERIFY]; AR witness/exhibit procedure

title: Documents, protected material and civilian witnesses
body: Army Act provisions govern summons, protected documents and commissions to examine witnesses, with procedural requirements. Sensitive operational records require both lawful evidentiary treatment and separate security controls. Map every witness and document to a proposition in issue. Use applicable military or civilian attendance procedure. Address lawful exemption/privilege claims with competent legal authority. Record chain of custody for documentary and physical exhibits. AA §§135–138; AR trial rules

title: Fitness to stand trial and adjournment
body: A court should not treat clear incapacity, illness or a substantial inability to participate as a harmless administrative issue. Section 117 explicitly addresses impossibility of continuation due to illness of accused or judge advocate. Document medical/fitness concern promptly. Seek competent medical and legal assessment. Use lawful adjournment or dissolution procedure as circumstances warrant. Keep the procedural record of safeguards and decisions. AA §117(2); AR rr56, adjournment provisions [exact rule verify]
references: AA §117(2); AR rr56, adjournment provisions [exact rule verify]

title: SCM special pleas and witness examination
body: SCM uses its own rule sequence and is not a GCM shortened by administrative choice. Rule 115 contains guilty-plea safeguards; Rule 116 governs subsequent procedure; Rule 118 deals with proceedings following not-guilty plea. Use only the authentic SCM record forms and applicable rule order. Explain and record each plea and any legally required correction. Ensure defence participation and witnesses as permitted. Maintain full record supporting finding and sentence. AR rr110–127; esp rr115–118

title: Voting, findings and benefit of tie
body: Decisions of multi-member courts are ordinarily by absolute majority, with tied findings or sentences resolved for the accused; death sentences have special concurrence thresholds. The SCM is constituted by its CO alone and not by a panel vote. Apply correct voting rule to correct court type. Ensure legally qualified membership at voting. Record official finding/sentence without disclosure of prohibited individual votes. Verify any mandatory special-majority threshold. AA §132; AR findings provisions

title: Sentence selection, legality and mitigation
body: The available sentence depends on offence maximum, court type, rank, limits and mitigation. The objective is lawful proportional sentencing, not an automated punishment recommendation. Identify maximum authorised offence sentence and available Section 71 penalties. Apply forum-specific ceiling and person-specific restrictions. Document mitigation and aggravation presented in proceedings. Verify legal form and confirmation requirements before execution. AA §71 and relevant maximum offence penalty; §§118–120,132; AR sentence provisions
references: AA §71 and relevant maximum offence penalty; §§118–120,132; AR sentence provisions

title: GCM/DCM/SGCM confirmation is essential
body: The finding and sentence of GCM, DCM or SGCM are not valid unless confirmed as provided by law. The competent confirming authority is governed by Sections 154–157 and the operative warrants, not by convenience or seniority alone. Identify confirming authority and any warrant conditions. Send complete proceedings for legally required review. Record confirmation, non-confirmation or authorised mitigation explicitly. Do not promulgate/execute as though confirmed before actual confirmation. AA §§153–159

title: Revision at confirming stage
body: Section 160 permits one revision of a finding or sentence requiring confirmation, with the same court members subject to limited absence exceptions and possible additional evidence where directed. This is distinct from an appeal or an unlimited retrial. Check actual confirmation status and power to direct revision. Review statutory one-revision restriction and membership continuity. Record any additional evidence and accused safeguards. Return complete revisional proceedings for proper confirmation. AA §160

title: SCM findings: approval exception, forwarding and review
body: SCM findings and sentences generally do not need confirmation and may take effect subject to Section 161(2) special approval requirement where the trial officer has under five years’ service outside active service. Proceedings must be forwarded and are subject to statutory review. Confirm years of service of officer holding SCM. Apply Section 161(2) approval exception if engaged. Handle promulgation under current authenticated AR rules. Forward proceedings promptly through prescribed channel for Section 162 review. AA §§161–162; AR rr131–133

title: Statutory petitions and annulment
body: Section 164 distinguishes challenges to orders and post-confirmation findings/sentences. Section 165 confers statutory annulment power on prescribed authorities for illegal or unjust proceedings. AFT exhaustion rules and time limits require separate analysis. Identify the impugned order, finding or sentence and confirmation status. Map which Section 164 route and competent recipient actually applies. Record service and communication dates and available AFT remedies. Preserve full original court record for independent review. AA §§164–165; AFT Act §21

title: AFT jurisdiction over court-martial appeals
body: Section 15 empowers AFT to hear court-martial appeals and grant prescribed relief, with grounds including legal errors and material irregularities resulting in miscarriage of justice. The service-matter definition has particular exclusions concerning some summary matters; route must be analysed carefully. Identify exact kind of action: court-martial appeal vs administrative service matter. Check Section 15 and statutory exclusions, jurisdiction and limitation. Check exhaustion requirement and applicable procedural rules. Compile documents and chronology with decisions/judgment paragraphs. AFT Act §§3(o),15–17,21–22

title: Re-trial after appeal and double jeopardy checks
body: AA Section 121 generally prohibits another court-martial or summary disposal for the same offence after specified acquittal, conviction or summary disposal. AFT Section 16 contains a narrowly framed retrial power after appeal; dissolution under AA Section 117 is a distinct situation. Locate all earlier decisions for same facts/offence. Determine whether prior outcome constitutes the statutory bar. Identify distinct grounds under Section 117 or AFT Section 16 before considering re-trial. Do not initiate fresh process solely because earlier outcome was inconvenient. AA §§117,121; AFT Act §16

title: Promulgation, custody and execution safeguards
body: Legal effect and execution depend on court type, confirmation/approval and promulgation requirements; sentence commencement may differ from date of administrative paperwork. Section 169A addresses credit for specified pre-trial custody. Identify precise sentence and date of original proceedings signature. Verify confirmation/approval/promulgation prerequisites. Compute custody credit under Section 169A where applicable with records. Issue only authorised warrants and notifications. AA §§161–162,167–169A; AR promulgation rules

title: Preservation, disclosure and appellate record
body: Appeal defensibility depends on an authentic complete record. Store original proceedings, all exhibits, notices, orders, legal review and transmission history as a controlled chain rather than an editable working file. Seal original signed proceedings in authorised registry. Maintain indexed copies with hashes, access logs and legal disclosure controls. Preserve exhibits and unredacted/authorised redacted versions separately. Retain JAG objections, confirmation and appellate correspondence. AA §§153–165; AFT Act §§15,17; AR proceeding rules
references: AA §§153–165; AFT Act §§15,17; AR proceeding rules

title: Classification, confidentiality and proposed AI use
body: A military-law assistant should be an indexed legal reference system first. Access to service records and evidence must follow classification, privacy and role-specific controls; no generative output should impersonate binding JAG advice. Create separate public-legislation and restricted/service-only corpus partitions. Use default deny for personnel and classified material; allow only authorised roles. Capture source/version and human JAG approval for each knowledge record. Log retrieval, changes and overrides; publish signed read-only snapshots to LAN. Source policy [AO not acquired]; AA/AR records; information security regulations [VERIFY]
references: Source policy [AO not acquired]; AA/AR records; information security regulations [VERIFY]

title: SCM proposed for a JCO
body: A JCO is alleged to have misused leave. CO asks whether he can hold an SCM. Verify service/rank and Section 120(3). SCM not authorised for officer/JCO/WO; identify lawful alternative and competent authority. Seek JAG and follow relevant Rule 22/26 route.

title: SCM proposed for soldier attached to another unit
body: An NCO commits an offence while on written attachment at a school. Collect attachment and command documents. Apply Section 116 and Vishav Priya Singh context. Record which CO had lawful command and seisin.

title: Section 69 allegation, no urgent action
body: Alleged civilian offence is being investigated for eight months before SCM proposed. Screen AA §§69,120(2),125–126. Document reasons, actual urgency and opportunity for superior-authority reference. Obtain JAG review before forum selection.

title: A GCM member below minimum service
body: One officer nominated to the five-member GCM has two years of commission. Check commission duration for each member. Apply Section 113 minimum and Rule 39 eligibility. Replace before commencement, using proper order.

title: Officers all belong to one corps
body: An officer accused in a GCM will face only members drawn from his corps. Apply Rule 40 and Prithi Pal Singh Bedi. Reconstitute if needed to satisfy legal requirement. Record reasons for lawful exception only if rule allows.
references: AR r40; Prithi Pal Singh Bedi

title: Accused objects to court member
body: Accused says a nominated member witnessed an incident and has prejudged it. Register objection and member response. Follow AA §130 and AR challenge sequence. Ensure challenge decided by proper remaining members and record result.

title: Defence gets papers late
body: Accused receives trial papers very late before court assembly. Audit service dates under current AR rr33–34. Provide lawful opportunity to prepare and consult. Record requests and adjudication; do not guess universal minimum.

title: Accused pleads guilty but denies intent
body: A charged soldier pleads guilty but claims the damage was entirely accidental. Test offence mental element and Rule 52/115 effect. Explain plea in legally prescribed manner. Alter/handle plea as rule directs if admission inconsistent with guilt.

title: One court member falls ill
body: During a three-member DCM one member permanently unavailable. Check statutory minimum and whether trial commenced. Apply AA §117 and applicable Rule 38. Do not add a replacement mid-trial without legal authority.

title: Limitation dispute
body: Wrongdoing discovered years after alleged act. Build dated offence/knowledge/identity chronology. Apply all branches of AA §122 and exceptions. Obtain a written legal calculation before forum selection.

title: Retired officer alleged to have offended on service
body: Officer retired last year; an old procurement allegation emerges. Check status at offence and exact cessation date. Separately calculate §§122 and 123. Request JAG before custody or trial steps.

title: Civil police and Army both claim jurisdiction
body: Civilian FIR filed against serving Army person. Analyse offence under AA §69 and special exclusions. Determine Section 125 competent authority; check criminal-court notice under §126. Preserve written correspondence and legal decisions.

title: GCM result sent to unit before confirmation
body: Personnel branch wants to implement sentence immediately. Check actual confirming authority and warrant. Apply §§153–157; withhold premature execution. Record final order and promulgate in lawful manner.

title: SCM held by officer with under five years service
body: Non-active-service SCM sentence proposed for immediate execution. Calculate trial officer service length. Apply Section 161(2) approval rule. Check AR promulgation and forwarding steps.

title: Repeated proceedings for same misconduct
body: Soldier punished under Section 80; proposed GCM on same alleged act. Compare precise offence and earlier disposal. Apply §121 and distinguish any truly separate offence. Seek legal view before any new trial.

title: AFT appeal after SCM
body: Dismissed soldier proposes legal challenge to SCM. Identify trial record, communication, statutory petitions. Apply AFT §15, §3(o) exclusions for service matters as relevant, and exhaustion/limitation. Preserve all exhibits and secure counsel/JAG assessment.

title: CCTV and server logs offered as trial evidence
body: Unit alleges that security footage and logs conclusively prove an act. Preserve original media and system timestamp details. Record chain of custody/hashes and a technical witness. Resolve current evidence-law requirements with JAG.

title: An order quotes old Section 127
body: An old manual says Section 127 permits successive civil and Army trials. Check India Code 2025 text showing §127 omitted in 1992. Apply live §§121,125,126. Correct obsolete template and flag as superseded.

title: Before choosing any court-martial
body: Identify accused rank/service status and command at material time Identify offence sections and particulars Screen civil jurisdiction and §125/126 Compute §§122–123 time bars Determine proper forum and limitations Locate actual convening warrant / legal CO authority Consult JAG and record sign-off

title: GCM/DCM convening checklist
body: Verify convening officer power and warrant Check Rule 37 review of offence and evidence Complete charge-sheet accuracy Audit Rule 33/34 defence supply and warning Select and screen legally eligible court members Nominate judge advocate as required Record signed convening order

title: GCM member screening
body: Commission duration/rank against §113 Membership count minimum Corps/department Rule 40 requirement Member involvement, bias and Rule 39 exclusions Sufficient ranks for officer accused Contemporaneous recorded availability/exception opinion Accused challenge opportunity §130

title: SCM legal gateway
body: CO legal command/attachment verified Accused not officer/JCO/WO §120(2) restricted offence screened Reference/urgency and Rule 130 record as required Trial officer rank and sentence cap Two qualifying non-sworn attendees identified Separate SCM rule forms selected

title: Pretrial rights and disclosure
body: Rule 22/SoE preceding records checked Charge-sheet delivered with proof Current rule-specific warning period verified Defence documents, assistance and witness access arranged Interpreter/fitness issues considered Any lawful exception documented Counsel/defending officer/friend status recorded

title: Opening trial proceedings
body: Convening order and charge-sheet presented Court checks legal constitution Competence of accused and offence checked Names of members and challenges handled Applicable oaths administered Plea recorded with understanding Objections ruled on and logged

title: Plea of guilty
body: Charge ingredients and language understood Statutory explanation and effect of plea Check inconsistency with record and defence statement Special bar where death penalty possible (GCM/DCM Rule 52) Guilty plea compliance recorded Evidence/SoE and mitigation under applicable rule Change plea if rule so requires

title: Trial exhibits and witnesses
body: Witness list and statutory summons Oath / exception handled Evidence with examination/cross-examination Exhibits numbered and authenticated Chain of custody preserved Defence witnesses/objections addressed Electronic evidence law version checked

title: Findings and sentence
body: Valid court strength maintained Correct forum-specific voting rule Evidence supports statutory elements Sentence within offence and court maxima Rank-specific restrictions and mitigation Findings/sentence signed and authenticated Confirmation/approval requirement identified

title: Post-GCM/DCM/SGCM
body: Complete proceedings forwarded to correct confirming authority Warrant restrictions verified Revision request under §160 handled once if applicable Actual confirmation noted Promulgation per authorised rules Sentence execution only upon legal readiness Petition and AFT documents preserved

title: Post-SCM
body: Officer under-five-service approval exception checked Record complete and signed Promulgation/implementation legally sequenced Proceedings forwarded under §162 Review findings and directions logged Custody/sentence calculation verified Original exhibits securely archived

title: Legal challenge / appellate readiness
body: Differentiate order vs finding/sentence Check §164 statutory petition route and status Check AFT §15 appeal / limitation and exhaustion Obtain certified proceedings Create paragraph-anchored legal issues Log all relief/orders and supersession Preserve confidential case material under role controls

title: Digital evidence retention
body: Preserve source media and acquisition metadata Calculate SHA-256 and source label Restrict mutation and maintain audit log Record witness/expert identity Identify any computer-evidence certification under applicable law Keep classified content inside authorised LAN Test disclosure and anonymisation rules

title: Lt Col Prithi Pal Singh Bedi v Union of India
body: Court composition, statutory qualification and challenge safeguards must be considered according to the proper legal definitions. Decision under historical rules; later amendments and subsequent precedents may affect details.
references: PPS discussion of Rule 40 and Section 130; verify official PDF pages before operational use

title: Union of India v Vishav Priya Singh
body: SCM is a drastic CO power; Sections 116/120 and superior-authority reference safeguards matter. SCM may in relevant facts be held by CO of attached unit. A later review on 16 Feb 2017 clarified prospective operation of reasons requirement from 5 July 2016; do not overgeneralise holding.
references: VISHAV paras 19–25 and conclusion (verify authenticated original)

title: Randhir Singh v Union of India
body: SC examined Section 120(2) with Vishav Priya Singh and review clarification; long delay can be material to legality of selecting SCM. Judgment turns on factual circumstances and precise Section 120 statutory category; reasons-recording rule clarified as prospective.

title: Union of India v Ex Sep Virendra Kumar
body: Rule 180 CoI safeguards and consequences for later disciplinary proceedings require context-sensitive legal analysis. Not every CoI procedural defect automatically invalidates later court-martial; do not treat compliance as dispensable.

title: The first classification: disciplinary, administrative or service decision
body: Do not equate an adverse administrative outcome with a court-martial sentence. Identify the legal purpose and source of power, the rank affected, the intended consequence and whether the order is stigmatic or punitive in substance. Describe the facts without prejudging guilt Identify whether a charge, retention review, censure, CR entry or ordinary service order is proposed Locate the controlling statute and policy for that precise action Record why the selected route is legally available Incident chronology Rank and service status Proposed decision and legal grounds Using censure to circumvent trial safeguards Calling a termination merely an ordinary posting decision

title: Central Government power under Section 19
body: Section 19 places central termination power with the Central Government, subject to the Act and rules. A unit CO cannot assume this power because the matter arose in his unit. Identify officer/personnel category Identify exact rule governing grounds and process Verify Central Government recommendation and decision route Ensure the actual order is made by the statutory authority Authority sheet Show-cause/defence where applicable Government decision CO purporting to dismiss an officer under Section 19 Citing section without subordinate rule

title: Section 20 and the limits of delegated dismissal/removal
body: Section 20 creates specified powers of dismissal/removal; the proper authority varies with status and statutory delegation. Rule 17 addresses notice safeguards and exceptions. Classify the person and sub-section invoked Prove the actual exercise/delegation of power Apply Rule 17 and preserve the notice/exception record Record the effective date in accordance with Rule 18 Competence warrant Notice and reply Approval and service record Assuming every superior can dismiss Dispensing with notice on verbal grounds

title: Discharge under Army Rule 13: rank, ground and authority
body: Rule 13 must be applied by category, specific ground, column 3 authority and column 4 manner of discharge. A rendered HTML/text extraction of its table is insufficient to prove a particular competent authority. Use an authenticated image or source table, not a malformed extraction Identify precise table category and limb Verify ground, medical or show-cause condition and authority Review amended tables, regulations and special decisions Service attestation/enrolment Correct table entry Authority certificate Medical board if relevant Applying a JCO entry to an OR case Relying on garbled extracted table cells

title: Rule 14: misconduct-based termination of an officer
body: Where trial is inexpedient or impracticable and retention undesirable, Rule 14 describes show-cause, reports, defence, recommendation and Central Government decision, with narrow exceptions. It cannot be used simply because proof of an offence may fail. Record legal basis and reasons for impracticability/inexpediency of trial Consider disclosure safeguards and authorised exceptions Obtain written explanation and recommendation as required Submit for Government decision without predetermining result Reasons for trial route decision Reports relied on Notice/defence COAS recommendation Central Government order Treating Rule 14 as a substitute for a weak criminal case Non-disclosure without basis

title: Rule 15: inefficiency and grounds other than misconduct
body: Rule 15 is a separate route from misconduct-based Rule 14. The reasons for non-retention, disclosure, explanation and competent decision must fit the rule and the operative policy. Determine whether the ground is genuine inefficiency rather than relabelled misconduct Identify adverse material considered Provide process and defence opportunity as applicable Route through COAS and Government as required Performance history Adverse particulars Notice and reply Government order Misconduct dressed as inefficiency Ignoring exceptions and reasons

title: Rule 15-A: medical release of officers
body: Medical invalidment is not an ordinary disciplinary option; Rule 15-A prescribes medical board findings, notification and petition process. Relevant medical rules and confidentiality protections also apply. Obtain proper medical board finding Serve statutory notice and advise petition right where required Check specialist authority and next-of-kin provisions Avoid speculative disability or pension outcomes Medical board proceedings Notice delivery proof Petition record Final release order Ignoring appeal/petition route Using censure or efficiency assessment instead of medical board

title: Rule 13-A: failure of specified course or examination
body: A failure to qualify at a required examination or course has a specific rule and show-cause process for officers; it is not automatically a finding of misconduct. Verify mandatory course/exam and time allowed Check retries, extensions and waivers Issue statutory show-cause through competent channel Route recommendation and Government decision Course notification Results Extension decisions Reply to notice Automatic dismissal on course failure Use of general misconduct route

title: Rule 17: notice and exceptions for Section 20 action
body: Rule 17 calls for communicating particulars and reasonable time for written defence except specified conviction/exigency circumstances; reliance on an exception must be documented and reported where required. Identify §20(1) or §20(3) authority Prepare allegations/particulars sufficient for response Record response, consideration and reasons Where exception claimed, preserve certification/report Show-cause Delivery acknowledgment Reply Reasoned consideration Exception certification Undocumented non-service Using conviction exception without qualifying conviction

title: Rule 18: effective dates; no retrospective discharge
body: The operative date depends on status and type of order; Rule 18 expressly excludes retrospective effective dates. Dates of signature, Gazette notification, delivery and relief may differ. Determine applicability of sub-rule 18(1), (2) or (3) Check any specified future effective date Record Gazette notification or actual relief as required Audit pay/service and discharge certificate implications Notification Diary of orders Last duty date Pay/benefit entries Backdating discharge Confusing date of order with date of effect

title: Distinguish warning, displeasure, censure and punishment
body: A descriptive label does not prove the form, competent authority or recordability of a warning or censure. Policy-defined gradations, thresholds and career effects are time-specific. Locate authenticated censure policy effective on incident and order dates Identify category and competent authority Verify notice, reasons, reply and recording rules Explain effect on promotion by applicable selection policy Censure policy/version Authority Show-cause Outcome and record Calling censure a statutory punishment without legal basis Assuming every censure affects promotion identically

title: Show-cause notices: sufficient particulars and fair consideration
body: A meaningful opportunity to answer allegations requires particulars and a fair assessment of the actual reply, unless a valid statutory exception applies. Mere issuance does not demonstrate consideration. Specify alleged acts and relied-upon authority Identify material to be disclosed and lawful exceptions Provide legally applicable response period Create a contemporaneous note assessing substantive reply Notice Relied-on records index Delivery proof Reply Consideration note Prejudged decision New undisclosed grounds in final order

title: Recordable censure and promotion inputs
body: A recordable censure may be considered under relevant Army promotion policies; its actual impact is policy- and board-specific. The Supreme Court disapproved an ordinary substitution of the Tribunal’s view of censure gradation. Confirm classification and period of recordability under actual policy Verify proper communication and statutory complaint history Identify selection policy effective on board date Avoid categorical assurance or automatic disqualification Original censure Policy in force Board date/criteria Complaint order Treating recordable censure as life-long automatic bar Ignoring valid policy provisions
references: Censure policy (authenticated version); Kuldeep Yadav paras 19,22–26

title: Confidential Report (CR/ACR): which scheme applies?
body: Army reporting arrangements and selection criteria are governed by Army-specific policies. Civilian ACR communication rules cannot automatically be imported without assessing the military legal scheme. Record commission type, batch, arm/service and reporting period Obtain applicable Army Order and MS circulars by effective date Check initiation/review/technical reporting criteria Review relevant judicial treatment and individual facts CR chain Policy edition Reporting periods Relevant representations Applying civil-service templates as if identical to Army policy Using superseded quantified policy
references: Army CR policy; Pooja Pal (2026), discussion of AO 45/2001

title: Communications of adverse CR material
body: Communication, redress and non-recommendation depend on the applicable Army policy. Sukhdev Singh refers to general public-servant ACRs and expressly arose outside military service; do not assume universal Army applicability. Classify report and adverse entry under Army instructions Identify communication and representation requirements Check policy in force and evidence of compliance Refer disputed legal applicability to JAG CR extracts Communication proof Representation Policy edition Assuming all gradings must be communicated as in civilian cadre Withholding where policy requires disclosure
references: Applicable Army CR/complaint policy; Sukhdev Singh (2013)

title: Selection Boards and comparative merit
body: Promotion to higher ranks depends on applicable selection instructions and fair consideration; courts generally do not replace a properly constituted board’s professional assessment absent legal defects. Identify board number, batch and zone Locate board policy and quantified instructions in force Verify eligible profile and correct comparison group Scrutinise objective procedural and record errors Board composition Eligibility roll Policy text Reckonable CR index Confusing eligibility with entitlement to promotion Substituting a non-expert merit score
references: Brig Nalin Kumar Bhatia v UOI (2020) paras 6–15

title: Reckonable CR period and cut-off decisions
body: The applicable policy and correct reckoning period matter; selective exclusion of CRs can vitiate consideration. The 2023 Nitisha-implementation ruling is fact-specific to women officers and the policies before the Court. Identify applicable branch/batch/board Record every CR and effective policy revision Check notified cut-off and exceptions Refer alleged discrimination or selective exclusion to JAG CR period list Board cut-off MS letters Prior judgments Applying specific women-officer directions as universal rule Omitting favourable reckonable reports

title: Permanent Commission and Short Service Commission selection
body: The Supreme Court examined comparative assessment, ACR methodology and fairness in SSCO-to-PC selection. Build an effective-date policy timeline rather than applying a single later judgment mechanically. Record appointment type and course/batch Identify historic and current PC policy Check CR collection and normalisation methodology Determine whether judgment specifically governs cohort Commission order Policy circulars CR summaries Board decision Assuming decision applies identically to all cadres Ignoring subsequent policy revisions
references: Lt Col Pooja Pal v UOI (24 Mar 2026)

title: Medical category and promotion/retention
body: A medical category affects service through relevant medical board and selection instructions, which must be authenticated. The Army Rules do not alone determine each career consequence. Verify board’s actual medical finding Locate category-specific policy for retention or promotion Check disability rights issues and reasonable accommodation where applicable Preserve reconsideration/petition channels Board documents Current medical instruction Promotion criteria Petitions Automatic discharge for every low medical category Using unverified disability entitlement
references: Applicable Army medical/selection policies; AR rr13,15-A

title: Statutory complaint by non-officer under Section 26
body: For persons other than officers, Section 26 prescribes an initial command complaint route and investigation/referral duties. The exact manner of complaint is specified by proper authority. Record status and whether attached to troop/company Select proper receiving officer or next superior where complained-of officer is recipient Investigate and preserve evidence or refer upward Document reasoned redress/recommendations Complaint Acknowledgement Investigation notes Orders and communication Complaining to officer complained against without escalation option Treating complaint as misconduct

title: Statutory complaint by officer under Section 27
body: An officer may complain to Central Government after due application to his commanding officer fails to obtain the redress sought, in manner specified by proper authority. Record due application and attempts to secure redress Verify authorised channel, format, time limit and representation policy Consolidate record relied upon and rebuttal fairly Track receipt, speaking order and communication Initial application Statutory complaint Forwarding endorsements Decision Skipping policy procedure without legal reason Delaying forwarding merely for disagreement

title: Grievance against the receiving command authority
body: For non-officers §26(2) explicitly directs complaint to next superior when the complained-of officer would otherwise be recipient. Officers have a distinct §27 route. Record complained-of officer and position in chain Apply proper complaint statute for rank Avoid conflict of interest and preserve secure forwarding Seek JAG if recusal or security problems arise Complaint route memo Service status Acknowledgements Routing complaint back solely to complained-of officer Unlawful obstruction of grievances

title: Redress of complaints: reasoned record and privacy
body: A grievance file should preserve dates, relevant material, responsible decision maker and outcome; access must be restricted to those lawfully entitled. This is a practical record-keeping principle, not an extra statutory time limit. Acknowledge and diarise Keep evidence and chronology Separate investigation from policy interpretation Communicate decision within prescribed process Receipt register Evidence index Decision Service/communication proof Inventing statutory decision deadlines Unauthorized circulation of medical or personal data

title: AFT jurisdiction: identify exclusions before filing
body: Section 3(o) includes many service conditions but expressly excludes specified orders under Army Act §18, transfer/posting, leave, and certain SCM matters, subject to exact text and controlling judicial interpretation. Classify challenged act and prayer separately Examine §3(o) inclusion/exclusion and §14/15 route Check applicable judicial interpretation Seek litigation counsel on forum if exclusion implicated Impugned decision Prayer/relief draft Jurisdiction note Counsel opinion Treating all administrative matters as AFT service matters Assuming excluded transfers must always lie in AFT

title: AFT exhaustion and limitation
body: Section 21 ordinarily requires available service remedies to have been pursued; six months without decision has significance under §21(2)(b). Under §22(1)(a) the ordinary period after a final rejecting order is six months, subject to §22(2) sufficient-cause provision. Record original order, remedy and disposal dates Identify correct §21(2) route Calculate §22 limitation using authenticated current law Obtain legal opinion on condonation and exceptional facts Original order Statutory complaint proof Final disposal Limitation calculation Mistaking six-month exhaustion window for general filing deadline Assuming condonation is automatic

title: Judicial review of censure: threshold for interference
body: Judicial interference with proportionality of an administrative penalty is exceptional; the Tribunal is not an ordinary merits appeal over the authority’s subjective assessment and should identify legally defensible exceptional grounds. Map allegations against evidence Determine competent authority and operative censure policy Examine procedural fairness and application of mind Assess proportionality with judgment’s threshold Show-cause Reply Competent order Complaint and AFT records Re-assessing degree of censure on general sympathy alone Ignoring factual admissions

title: Judicial review of promotion: limits and exceptions
body: Court review generally examines legality and fairness, not military professional merit afresh. Exceptions turn on discrimination, arbitrariness, wrong policy, wrong data, bias or other legal defect. Assemble policy timeline Test all reckonable records and criteria Assess equality and procedural compliance Avoid promising court-directed promotion instead of fair consideration Policy and board records Batch list CR set Representations Asking judge to act as Selection Board Ignoring documented wrong criteria

title: Records for litigation: proof, not narrative
body: Chronological, authenticated, legible and privacy-controlled records are more reliable than retrospective narrative. Distinguish factual record from internal privileged legal advice. Preserve original orders, versioned policies and approvals Index evidence with dates and provenance Produce accurate chronology and annexures Restrict sensitive service and medical records Authenticated original Receipt and dispatch proof Indexed annexures Hash manifests Creating post-hoc purported contemporaneous notes Exposing private personnel data in public model

title: No retrospective application of revised policy without authority
body: Determine whether a revised policy states an effective date, transitional coverage or retrospective application. Rule 18 separately bars retrospective service-termination effective dates; do not confuse the two concepts. Record incident/decision/board dates Find policy notification and effective-date clause Review transitional rule Seek interpretation rather than assume newest is universal Earlier policy Amending policy Effective-date memo Conflating operative-date of policy with date of service order Inventing retrospectivity

title: Administrative decision versus hidden criminal accusation
body: Administrative authority is not a blank cheque to record criminal guilt without trial. Labels, evidence and civil/military jurisdiction must be assessed independently. Identify whether factual finding asserts an offence or retention concern Avoid recording unsupported guilt findings Select appropriate legal process and safeguards Send criminal or serious security matters for JAG scrutiny CoI record Allegation map Jurisdiction note Finding criminal guilt solely in a censure order Using administrative route to evade statutory protections

title: Documenting proportionality and parity
body: The decision-maker should link the actual facts, seriousness, mitigation and authorised gradation to a defensible decision. Judicial review is not ordinarily a re-sentencing exercise. Summarise relevant acts and applicable policy Consider explanations and material mitigation Assess comparable legally relevant cases, if available Record reasons linked to authority and policy Evidence table Response assessment Outcome rationale Ignoring mitigation entirely Using unevidenced claims of uniformity

title: Policies and delegation: do not infer competence
body: A legal assistant must display evidence of current competent authority rather than guessing from the office title. Internal orders and delegation schedules may be dispositive. Identify action type and affected category Locate formal delegation/warrant and effective dates Check whether statutory authority is reserved higher Block workflow if competence document missing Signed delegation Authority registry entry Source version and hash Automated inference of competence from rank alone Using expired delegation
references: AR r13 table; AR rr14–17; relevant service instructions

title: Court of Inquiry findings and subsequent administrative action
body: CoI findings are a fact-finding input and do not themselves replace applicable notice, evidence review and competent administrative decision. Rule 180 may matter if reputation is affected. Check CoI jurisdiction and safeguards Identify which findings are supported by evidence Review independent basis for proposed action Complete proper notice and competent decision route CoI proceedings Rule 180 participation record Action note Notice/decision Treating CoI as conviction Skipping follow-on rights

title: Service records and data sensitivity in offline system
body: Individual disciplinary, medical and confidential records require access controls, audit history, provenance and need-to-know restrictions. Public model notes and personal case data must remain separated. Classify source document and record sensitivity Capture source hash, edition, approver, validity period Enforce role-based access and redaction Keep model-generated text as a draft never a signed order Metadata RBAC decision Audit logs Source hashes Putting PII in general prompt corpus Treating generated advice as JAG approval

title: CO wants to award recordable censure
body: Fictional training scenario. A Major is blamed in a CoI; the CO assumes he may award Severe Displeasure (Recordable). Locate competent censure authority and the dated policy; verify notice, Rule 180 if relevant, and permissible gradation. Do not automatically award censure. Locate authenticated censure policy effective on incident and order dates Identify category and competent authority Verify notice, reasons, reply and recording rules Explain effect on promotion by applicable selection policy

title: Officer service proposed for termination due to misconduct
body: Fictional training scenario. An officer faces a serious allegation; court-martial is said to be inconvenient. AR r14 requires a real legally supportable trial-inexpediency/impracticability assessment; Government decision and due process. Record legal basis and reasons for impracticability/inexpediency of trial Consider disclosure safeguards and authorised exceptions Obtain written explanation and recommendation as required Submit for Government decision without predetermining result

title: Inefficiency labelled as misconduct
body: Fictional training scenario. An officer’s slow project output is called misconduct with no identified military offence. Separate inefficiency Rule 15 from Rule 14 misconduct; verify actual reason and policy. Determine whether the ground is genuine inefficiency rather than relabelled misconduct Identify adverse material considered Provide process and defence opportunity as applicable Route through COAS and Government as required

title: JCO discharge under generic order
body: Fictional training scenario. A unit forwards a JCO discharge and cites only “AR 13”. Verify the precise Rule 13 table row, manner and competent authority using authenticated image, not search snippets. Use an authenticated image or source table, not a malformed extraction Identify precise table category and limb Verify ground, medical or show-cause condition and authority Review amended tables, regulations and special decisions

title: Backdated removal
body: Fictional training scenario. Personnel branch proposes removal date six months before signed order. Rule 18 bars retrospective termination/discharge; check Gazette/actual effect rules. Determine applicability of sub-rule 18(1), (2) or (3) Check any specified future effective date Record Gazette notification or actual relief as required Audit pay/service and discharge certificate implications

title: Complaint against company commander
body: Fictional training scenario. A Havildar says his company commander refused to receive his complaint. AA §26(2) enables escalation to the next superior when respondent is normal receiver. Record status and whether attached to troop/company Select proper receiving officer or next superior where complained-of officer is recipient Investigate and preserve evidence or refer upward Document reasoned redress/recommendations

title: Officer statutory complaint remains undecided
body: Fictional training scenario. A Captain submitted a proper statutory complaint eight months ago. Review §27 route and AFT §21(2)(b) exhaustion; calculate §22 limitation carefully. Record due application and attempts to secure redress Verify authorised channel, format, time limit and representation policy Consolidate record relied upon and rebuttal fairly Track receipt, speaking order and communication

title: Posting order challenged in AFT
body: Fictional training scenario. A posted officer wants to challenge station change on compassionate grounds. AFT §3(o) expressly excludes transfers/postings; check controlling case-law and alternative forum. Classify challenged act and prayer separately Examine §3(o) inclusion/exclusion and §14/15 route Check applicable judicial interpretation Seek litigation counsel on forum if exclusion implicated

title: Civil ACR rule used for Army officer
body: Fictional training scenario. An advocate relies solely on Sukhdev Singh to assert every Army CR must be furnished. Apply current Army CR policy and distinguish civilian ACR ruling. Classify report and adverse entry under Army instructions Identify communication and representation requirements Check policy in force and evidence of compliance Refer disputed legal applicability to JAG
references: Applicable Army CR/complaint policy; Sukhdev Singh (2013)

title: Single eligible officer demands automatic promotion
body: Fictional training scenario. A Brigadier is only eligible candidate for a Selection Board. Eligibility alone does not guarantee empanelment; examine board policy and fair assessment. Identify board number, batch and zone Locate board policy and quantified instructions in force Verify eligible profile and correct comparison group Scrutinise objective procedural and record errors
references: Brig Nalin Kumar Bhatia v UOI (2020) paras 6–15

title: Promotion profile cutoff disputed
body: Fictional training scenario. Two comparison groups have different end dates for CR inclusion. Use operative MS instructions, exact cutoff and the 2023 Nitisha implementation decision cautiously. Identify applicable branch/batch/board Record every CR and effective policy revision Check notified cut-off and exceptions Refer alleged discrimination or selective exclusion to JAG

title: PC selection grading differences
body: Fictional training scenario. Short-service male and women officers were assessed under non-identical regimes. Verify Lt Col Pooja Pal (2026) applicability, cohort and selected remedy. Record appointment type and course/batch Identify historic and current PC policy Check CR collection and normalisation methodology Determine whether judgment specifically governs cohort
references: Lt Col Pooja Pal v UOI (24 Mar 2026)

title: CoI used as final disciplinary verdict
body: Fictional training scenario. CO writes that CoI “found guilty” and issues censure without hearing reply. CoI is fact-finding; do separate legally applicable process and ensure actual authority. Check CoI jurisdiction and safeguards Identify which findings are supported by evidence Review independent basis for proposed action Complete proper notice and competent decision route

title: Court asked to reduce censure on sympathy
body: Fictional training scenario. An officer had exemplary service but admitted sustained misconduct. Apply Kuldeep Yadav exceptional proportionality threshold; focus on actual legal defect. Map allegations against evidence Determine competent authority and operative censure policy Examine procedural fairness and application of mind Assess proportionality with judgment’s threshold

title: Confidential case file uploaded to search
body: Fictional training scenario. Adjutant imports unredacted ACRs and medical record into general searchable notes. Keep individual cases segregated, role-controlled, audited and outside public explanatory corpus. Classify source document and record sensitivity Capture source hash, edition, approver, validity period Enforce role-based access and redaction Keep model-generated text as a draft never a signed order

title: Classify action before drafting any order
body: Identify affected person and legal status Identify proposed adverse consequence Name enabling Act/rule and current policy Identify competent authority Preserve factual chronology

title: Officer termination under Rule 14 or Rule 15
body: Distinguish misconduct from inefficiency Confirm Government authority and rule Document prerequisites and mandatory notice Record reports/defence and COAS recommendation Confirm operative date and service benefits

title: Discharge under Rule 13
body: Obtain authenticated current four-column table Identify category and exact discharge ground Verify board or show-cause requirements Confirm actual authority and effective date Complete discharge certificate and benefits

title: Censure and warning
body: Locate current dated Army censure instructions Check who may issue specific gradation Identify fair process and evidence Assess reply and mitigation Determine recordability and policy effect

title: CR and promotion audit
body: Identify course/batch/board number Verify effective date policy and CR rules Index reckonable and excluded CRs Record board data and reason for exclusions Review complaint and judicial remedy

title: Army Act section 26/27 grievance
body: Identify officer or non-officer Select correct receiving channel Obtain complaint and supporting records Provide fair investigation or referral Track decision and service

title: AFT forum, exhaustion and limitation
body: Classify §3(o) exclusions Check §14 or §15 jurisdiction Record remedies and dates per §21 Compute §22 limitation and condonation facts Take counsel/JAG opinion

title: Evidence and record chain
body: Separate source original from notes Record document hash and version Create event chronology Redact personal/sensitive details as authorised Preserve audit trail

title: Mandatory JAG approval before action
body: Verify no legal authority has been guessed Check amendment and effective date Prove delegated competence Review actual legal risk and remedies Sign off legally relevant answer and source version

title: Union of India & Ors v Lt Col Kuldeep Yadav
body: The AFT may review proportionality but interference with the competent authority’s censure gradation is constrained; Supreme Court restored Severe Displeasure (Recordable). Policy and misconduct were case-specific; do not extrapolate an all-purpose censure scale or automatic career outcome.

title: Union of India v Harjeet Singh Sandhu
body: A time bar on court-martial proceedings does not by itself invalidate a separately authorised §19/Rule 14 process. Rule 14 jurisdictional and fair-process prerequisites still control; official-text validation pending.
references: judgment discussion of AA §19, AR r14 and §122

title: Brig Nalin Kumar Bhatia v Union of India
body: Army Selection Boards evaluate overall reckonable profile under operative policy; judicial scrutiny tests fair consideration/legal defects, not substitution of expert merit view. Policy and candidate comparison factors case-specific.

title: MA 1913/2022, Nitisha implementation
body: Army must apply its own operative CR reckoning criteria fairly in PC-to-Colonel promotion review of affected women officers. Directions tied to specific case, cohorts and policy; not a universal nine-year rule.

title: Lt Col Pooja Pal & Ors v Union of India
body: Supreme Court reviewed ACR assessment methodology and fairness in competitive PC consideration for affected SSCOs. The exact dispositive directions must be checked in full before using case as an operational rule.
