references: paras 8–10 and operative directions (verify full text)

title: Which pension code applies to this individual?
body:
Question: An Army pension claim may refer to 1961, 2008 or 2023 instruments: which is operative?
Legal position: Start with service, applicable pension regulations and incident/retirement dates. The 2008 PRA preface states a temporal scope and continues earlier provisions where not governed; the 2023 entitlement scheme has a separate casualty-claim commencement rule.
Checks: Record enrolment, discharge, retirement, invalidment, death and claim dates separately.; Identify Army/DSC/TA/SSC status and rank category.; Find the specific regulation, government sanction and amendments applicable to each benefit.; Do not use a current explainer to rewrite a historically accrued entitlement.
Records: Service book; PPO and revisions; discharge certificate; government sanction date; medical board/casualty date
Risks: No single statute governs every retired cohort; Later policy may be prospective; Current FAQ does not replace operative order
Example: A soldier discharged in 2002 and a soldier injured in 2025 cannot be compared without identifying distinct source periods.

title: Rule, regulation, policy letter and explanatory FAQ
body:
Question: Can I determine a pension rate from a ministry web summary?
Legal position: Official explanatory web pages are navigational aids; the legal answer must trace to a pension regulation, sanctioned letter and current revision table. Later judicial directions may affect interpretation and a bare summary can be stale.
Checks: Identify instrument type and issuing authority.; Preserve title, date, URL, version and amendment relation.; Check circular register for revision or corrigendum.; Escalate conflicts to authorised legal/finance branch.
Records: Original order PDF; amendment chain; PPO history; pension slip
Risks: Never treat an FAQ as amending a regulation; Avoid copying a payment rate from an undated webpage

title: Critical event chronology
body:
Question: Why are multiple event dates necessary?
Legal position: Entitlement, calculation, revision, arrears and appellate time limits can depend on different legal trigger dates. A single "date of retirement" field cannot represent the case.
Checks: Create event fields for enrolment, injury/disease onset, report date, medical-board date, discharge/retirement, claim, rejection communication, appeal, PPO revision, OROP effective date.; Record source evidence for each date.; Label disputed dates.
Records: Casualty report; service book; board minutes; postal/digital communication; PPO
Risks: Do not backdate evidence to fit eligibility; Avoid applying 2023 ER solely from pension payment date

title: Service category matters
body:
Question: Do special rules apply to DSC, Territorial Army or short service commissions?
Legal position: PRA Part I identifies service categories in its scope. Different entry/engagement and qualifying service rules may apply. Case law on DSC second pension warns against mechanically importing a regular-Army result.
Checks: Classify service career(s) separately.; Record rank, regular service and subsequent DSC/TA career.; Verify relevant Part I regulation and other sanction.; Identify judicial decision limited to that group.
Records: Attestation/service records for each career; DSC re-enrolment order; qualifying-service statement
Risks: Combining two careers without legal authority; Applying officer pension threshold to PBOR

title: Service pension: qualifying service
body:
Question: Is a departing officer or PBOR eligible for service pension?
Legal position: DESW describes ordinary minimum qualifying service as 20 years for commissioned officers and 15 years for PBOR. These are broad defaults only; actual calculation must examine qualifying service, service category, exceptions and amendments.
Checks: Check rank/service category and mode of release.; Compute qualifying rather than raw calendar service.; Identify exclusions, forfeiture, condonation and re-employment.; Check whether a gratuity or invalid award rather than service pension applies.
Records: Service statement with days; non-qualifying service orders; release authority; PPO
Risks: A nominal 15/20 years rule is not a decision for atypical careers; Do not conflate qualifying and reckonable emoluments

title: Counting interruptions and forfeiture
body:
Question: What happens to interrupted or forfeited service?
Legal position: PRA Part I distinguishes service that qualifies, interruption/condonation and forfeiture. The actual penalty, break and subsequent restoration must be identified before calculating a final qualifying-service result.
Checks: List all service periods chronologically.; Map interruption/absence/forfeiture orders to governing regulation.; Check condonation authority; do not assume automatic benefit.; Obtain Accounts verification.
Records: Service register; forfeiture/remission records; Accounts verification; condonation correspondence
Risks: Do not count service after a forfeiture without restoration; Do not convert calendar years directly into qualifying-service years

title: Condonation of deficient service
body:
Question: Can a small shortfall be condoned for pension?
Legal position: PRA Part I contains condonation mechanisms. The 2026 Supreme Court in Balakrishnan Mullikote examined DSC shortfall and held executive letters cannot override clear regulations; applicability must be linked to specific category and period.
Checks: Calculate the precise deficiency in years/months/days.; Identify exact regulation and competent authority.; Check whether an order unlawfully narrows a regulation.; Seek legal/Accounts opinion in contested cases.
Records: Certified qualifying service; condonation request; impugned rejection; applicable letters
Risks: Do not say all shortfalls are condonable; Do not extend DSC ruling automatically to every service category

title: Reckonable emoluments and pension computation
body:
Question: Which pay components count for pension?
Legal position: Pension rates turn on "reckonable emoluments" and approved pay structures, not gross pay or take-home salary. The official DESW overview explains ordinary pension calculations but is not a self-contained rate engine.
Checks: Obtain last pay certificate and component schedule.; Apply rank/cadre/period-specific reckonable-emoluments rules.; Compare sanctioned calculation with PPO and revised orders.; Check rounding, minimum/maximum and DA/DR only after eligibility.
Records: LPC; pay statements; Government pay orders; PPO
Risks: Do not include non-reckonable allowances by intuition; No automatic amount without live pay tables

title: Gratuity versus pension
body:
Question: If minimum pension service is not met, what alternatives require examination?
Legal position: Retiring/service gratuity and retirement gratuity are distinct from recurring pension and may be governed by separate conditions. Each award requires its own qualifying-service and mode-of-exit analysis.
Checks: Classify service gratuity, retiring gratuity, retirement gratuity separately.; Test relevant regulation and personnel category.; Check disciplinary consequences and previous service.; Match each sanctioned award to PPO/service records.
Records: Service particulars; gratuity calculation sheet; nomination; Accounts sanction
Risks: Do not confuse retirement gratuity with service gratuity; Premature exit can alter entitlement

title: Voluntary premature retirement
body:
Question: Does leaving early preserve all benefits?
Legal position: Retirement on request may affect pension eligibility or disability-related benefits differently from retirement at tenure or invalidment. Relevant government letters and effective dates must be applied case by case.
Checks: Capture resignation/premature release authority and date.; Check qualifying service and pension regulation.; Check applicable disability scheme and special circulars.; Do not assume a medical condition automatically equals invalidment.
Records: Release order; retirement request; medical classification; applicable government letter
Risks: Do not treat premature retirement as invalidment; Do not grant impairment relief without required medical-board route

title: DSC second service pension
body:
Question: A DSC veteran has short second-service qualifying service. What must be reviewed?
Legal position: The 2026 Balakrishnan Mullikote decision reviewed regulations governing qualifying DSC service and condonation. The specific outcome depends on second-service dates, regulations, shortfall and actual final order.
Checks: Record regular Army and DSC periods separately.; Compute DSC qualifying service and precise shortfall.; Read PRA provision and the 2026 judgment.; Determine whether refusal rests only on an inconsistent executive circular.
Records: Regular Army PPO; DSC service book; shortfall calculation; government letters
Risks: Do not claim a universal second pension; Relevant 1961 versus 2008 period is decisive

title: Retirement handover checklist
body:
Question: What does a CO need to verify before individual proceeds on retirement?
Legal position: A unit can prevent downstream pension disputes by checking service, identity, nomination, medical board and documentation in advance. This is an editorial administrative checklist requiring current Record Office instructions.
Checks: Reconcile service dates with Accounts records.; Confirm dependant and nomination details.; Complete required medical board/records.; Track claim receipt and PPO issuance.; Provide SPARSH access support.
Records: Service book; nomination and family register; medical records; benefit claim; PPO acknowledgement
Risks: Do not promise an award not sanctioned; Sensitive family data requires controlled access

title: 2023 entitlement rules: commencement
body:
Question: Does the 2023 disability scheme govern an earlier pensioner?
Legal position: The official DESW FAQ and PIB clarification say ER/GMO 2023 apply to death and disability reported/recorded after 21 September 2023 and do not disturb existing pensioners receiving benefits. Actual effective operation must also be tested against original government order.
Checks: Determine date the casualty/disability was recorded/reported.; Identify original pension regime and award already sanctioned.; Match current claim to old entitlement versus a fresh event.; Use 2023 terminology only when applicable.
Records: Initial incident report; medical board date; PPO/old sanction; ER 2023 order
Risks: Do not apply 2023 mechanically to pre-2023 award; Do not infer new claim only from a post-2023 appeal date
references: V6-S04|MoD letter dated 21 Sep 2023 | V6-S05|Q1-3 | V6-S06|para 27

title: Attributable, aggravated and NANA
body:
Question: Who determines causal relationship to military service?
Legal position: The 2023 medical guide distinguishes medical assessment of impairment from entitlement decisions after examining medical and non-medical evidence. Attributable, aggravated and neither-attributable-nor-aggravated are separate findings, not a unit commander’s informal opinion.
Checks: Identify diagnosis and onset.; Collect exposure/duty/place-of-posting records.; Obtain board reasons for causal connection or its absence.; Locate competent entitlement authority and appeal channel.
Records: Medical board proceedings; injury/casualty report; service postings; treatment history
Risks: No unexplained label "NANA"; Do not equate occurrence during service with proven service causation
references: V6-S07|Chapter I paras 2-9; Chapter II para 1 | V6-S04|Entitlement Rule 2023 original check

title: Medical board versus competent authority
body:
Question: Can the CO certify percentage disability or final entitlement?
Legal position: Medical boards assess clinical impairment and provide reasoned medical opinions; competent authorities decide entitlement within the governing scheme. The unit supplies contemporaneous facts but does not replace medical or pension sanctioning authorities.
Checks: Secure medical board type/approval details.; Verify board assessment and attribution reasoning.; Identify separate entitlement decision and pension sanction.; Allow review/appeal where indicated.
Records: IMB/RMB/other applicable board; approval endorsement; entitlement sanction/rejection
Risks: Do not alter a medical assessment administratively; Do not treat a board diagnosis alone as an entitlement award
references: V6-S07|Chapter I paras 3-8; Medical Boards chapter

title: Invalided versus deemed invalided
body:
Question: Does low medical classification alone make someone invalided?
Legal position: 2023 FAQ distinguishes actual invalidment before completion of engagement and "deemed invalidment" for specified PBOR discharges. It expressly states deemed invalidment does not apply to officers.
Checks: Determine status and terms of engagement.; Verify reason for discharge and efforts regarding alternative suitable employment.; Check applicable retention orders.; Obtain board and competent-authority documents.
Records: Discharge and invalidment orders; LM category record; alternative employment documents; board proceedings
Risks: Never treat all low-medical category personnel as invalided; Never extend deemed invalidment to officers

title: Disability pension versus impairment relief
body:
Question: Is a retiring officer with accepted disability awarded the same benefit as invalided personnel?
Legal position: ER 2023 differentiates composite disability pension for invalided personnel (service plus disability elements) from impairment relief for eligible personnel retained in service and later retiring normally. The change is not a general cut in rates according to DESW.
Checks: Check invalidment status.; If retained, find appropriate impairment/retention medical-board process.; Check capitalised versus periodic impairment choice and whether already elected.; Apply pension/gratuity separately.
Records: RIAMB/RIAB documents; retention order; choice/award records; PPO
Risks: Do not award both incompatible capitalised and monthly benefits; Do not use "disability pension" generically for every retained retiree

title: Immediate injury-report procedure
body:
Question: A soldier is injured in training: what should the unit preserve?
Legal position: GMO 2023 treats the injury report as a primary contemporaneous document relevant to cause and attributable status. The later pension authority needs reliable duty circumstances, not a retrospective assertion unsupported by records.
Checks: Arrange treatment and preserve clinical record.; Make prompt initial incident and injury report through authorised channel.; Collect duty roster, orders, witnesses and event timeline.; Document whether person was on bona fide duty and causal connection.; Forward complete set to the Record Office/medical authorities.
Records: Injury Report; hospital admission sheet; duty order; witness statements; incident chronology
Risks: Avoid drafting the injury story months later; Do not fabricate a causal nexus to improve award
references: V6-S07|Chapter II para 2; Chapter III evidentiary guidance

title: Non-battle versus battle casualties
body:
Question: Does the term battle casualty decide pension by itself?
Legal position: Classification, causation, approved casualty category and pension sanction are related but distinct. Government rules identify categories and award types. The administrative label alone is not a substitute for category/entitlement determination.
Checks: Determine operation/training/leave facts.; Check relevant casualty classification order.; Record contemporaneous SITREP and incident evidence.; Identify competent authority and relevant category.
Records: Battle casualty report; SITREP; operational tasking; medical/injury report
Risks: Do not promise liberalised family pension because an event was called a battle casualty; Do not confuse operational classification with medical disability assessment
references: V6-S04|2023 categories (text verify) | V6-S06|paras 41-49 | V6-S07|injury evidence paras

title: Injury while on leave or in transit
body:
Question: Does an accident on leave necessarily qualify as attributable to military service?
Legal position: A service nexus is a fact-and-rule inquiry; mere service status or timing on leave does not automatically prove a duty-connected accident. Exact leave, movement order, duty circumstances, and governing rule are essential.
Checks: Record purpose and authorised movement.; Collect leave pass, movement orders and exact accident location.; Obtain contemporaneous police/hospital records.; Refer causal question to competent authority with evidence.
Records: Leave certificate; travel orders/tickets; FIR where any; medical and witness records
Risks: No automatic denial solely for being on leave; No automatic grant solely because individual was serving

title: Disease diagnosed during service
body:
Question: Is every disease first observed in service attributable?
Legal position: The 2019 N S Yadav judgment rejects mechanical application of the no-disease-at-enrolment presumption in its factual context. GMO 2023 requires a reasoned nexus inquiry; historical precedent must be analysed under the applicable historical scheme.
Checks: Compare enrolment medical documentation with later diagnosis.; Identify known onset date and exposures.; Review reasoned medical-board attribution.; Examine whether case is governed by pre-2023 rules or ER2023.
Records: Enrolment medical report; treatment progression; posting/duty history; board reasons
Risks: Do not mechanically treat all mental illness as service-attributable; Do not assume peace posting automatically rules out service impact

title: Multiple disabilities and assessment
body:
Question: How should combined assessments be handled?
Legal position: Clinical composite assessments and individual accepted impairments can affect benefits. Percentages cannot simply be added or broad-banded without following the relevant medical-board rules and award category.
Checks: Obtain accepted and nonaccepted impairment details.; Verify medical composite assessment methodology.; Check whether award had previous capitalised settlement.; Apply corresponding compensation category only after eligibility.
Records: Medical board assessment tables; previous disability award; reassessment order; PPO
Risks: Never sum disability percentages arithmetically; Do not treat percentage as proving causation
references: V6-S07|Medical Board chapter; Chapter VII | V6-S11|broad-banding circular

title: Broad-banding: threshold and eligibility
body:
Question: Is a disability percentage automatically rounded to 50/75/100?
Legal position: The 27 December 2023 MoD letter sets out broad-banding criteria, and Ram Avtar is significant for eligible completion-of-tenure retirees. However eligibility, type of impairment and governing circular must be resolved before applying a band.
Checks: Check legal award and whether the disability is accepted.; Determine whether scheme is invalidment, completion of tenure or war injury.; Read 2023 circular and contemporaneous government instructions.; Record both medically assessed and reckonable percentage; do not substitute one for the other.
Records: Accepted percentage; award sanction; 2023 circular; PPO
Risks: No universal rounding for all medical impairment; No automatic award if basic entitlement fails

title: Invalid pension where NANA
body:
Question: What if invalidment is neither attributable nor aggravated?
Legal position: DESW confirms that invalid pension may be available for qualifying NANA invalidments; it notes the 16 July 2020 modification removing the former ten-year condition for specified personnel in service on/after 4 January 2019. Verify exact sanction rather than reading the FAQ alone.
Checks: Verify true invalidment and medical classification.; Identify NANA finding and applicability date.; Check specific 2020 government letter and benefit conditions.; Consider alternate gratuity and family protection.
Records: Invaliding medical board; date of service; relevant MoD sanction; qualifying service
Risks: A zero-year rule is not universal across time; Do not confuse NANA invalid pension and A/AG disability pension

title: War injury awards
body:
Question: What is different for a service member wounded in warlike operations?
Legal position: War injury element and liberalised disability structures are distinct from ordinary disability pension. The award depends on accepted injury category, disability and whether invalided or later discharged.
Checks: Determine correct category with dated authority.; Check medical board, accepted degree and retirement status.; Separate war injury and ordinary service pension components.; Use current government rate order and PPO.
Records: Operational report; casualty classification; medical board; award decision
Risks: Do not use the normal disability rate in a war injury case; Do not promise a fixed percentage without effective date

title: Capitalised impairment relief and choice
body:
Question: What if an individual is retained with a permanent impairment?
Legal position: PIB describes capitalised impairment relief after appropriate retention-cum-impairment assessment; a later monthly impairment relief may be linked to foregoing the capitalised award, subject to the scheme.
Checks: Check medical-board certification and retention order.; Confirm election and whether a lump-sum has already been paid.; Assess potential interaction with monthly relief.; Do not offer a personal financial choice without full rules and competent advice.
Records: Board proceedings; sanction of capitalised award; election/consent; PPO history
Risks: No double grant of mutually exclusive awards; Do not infer options without official scheme text

title: Ordinary, special and liberalised family pension
body:
Question: Family of a deceased soldier requests pension; which category applies?
Legal position: Ordinary family pension is not the same as special family pension for a service-attributable/aggravated death or liberalised family pension for approved high-risk operational categories. Classify death and eligible dependant before computing award.
Checks: Record date, cause and circumstances of death.; Check service nexus and classification with competent authority.; Determine family eligibility under applicable regulation.; Obtain PPO, nomination and income/age records as needed.
Records: Death certificate; casualty reports; family particulars; PPO; entitlement sanction
Risks: Do not determine special family pension only from death in uniform; Do not assume nominal spouse is only potentially eligible claimant

title: Death attributable to service
body:
Question: What documentation supports special family pension?
Legal position: Service-attributable/aggravated death requires the relevant causal inquiry under the applicable rules. Contemporaneous cause, treatment and duty facts are crucial to equitable determination.
Checks: Open casualty case and preserve event evidence.; Obtain death certificate and medical cause of death.; Record duty and operational circumstances.; Ensure claim reaches competent authority with attachments.
Records: Medical certificate of cause of death; post-mortem if held; duty roster; casualty report; service history
Risks: No post facto fabrication of entitlement narrative; No automatic A/AG solely due to death while serving

title: Family pension to spouse and children
body:
Question: Which family member may qualify and for what duration?
Legal position: PRA Part I sets out eligible family definitions, sequence and duration, including provisions concerning eligible children and dependent parents. Personal law and family status questions require documentary verification.
Checks: Identify spouse, children, parents and any statutory competing claim.; Locate relevant award and cohort-specific definitions.; Verify ages, dependency, disability and marital status where legally required.; Escalate disputed relationship or rival claims.
Records: Nomination register; marriage documents; birth records; dependancy evidence; court orders if relevant
Risks: Nomination does not always settle statutory eligibility; Never disclose family records beyond authorised need

title: Children with disability and dependent parents
body:
Question: What happens where a child is disabled or parents are dependent?
Legal position: PRA contains specific provisions for disabled children and eligible parents; later amendments may modify eligibility or income thresholds. Individual status must be determined under the current order.
Checks: Determine child/dependent status with medical certificate if required.; Verify current income/age rules and order dates.; Record existing family pension recipient and change events.; Seek legal adjudication for conflicting claims.
Records: Disability certificate; birth proof; income certificate; pension sanction
Risks: Do not quote old monetary limits without current orders; No automatic exclusion solely based on age

title: Missing pensioner or service person
body:
Question: Can family pension begin when pensioner is missing?
Legal position: PRA includes provisions on missing personnel/pensioners. Case processing requires evidence of disappearance, reports and completion of procedural conditions; family entitlement differs from declaring death automatically.
Checks: Record last seen date and report.; Follow current missing-person claim procedure.; Collect police and competent-authority documents.; Preserve interim versus final payment record.
Records: Missing complaint/FIR; nontraceable report where required; family details; relevant sanction
Risks: Do not create a fictional death certificate; Do not promise immediate award without prescribed conditions

title: Suicide or disputed cause of death
body:
Question: Is family pension automatically unavailable after suicide?
Legal position: PRA Part I expressly covers ordinary family pension in suicide cases; the service-related casualty category, if claimed, needs careful separate inquiry. Avoid a blanket statement disqualifying the family.
Checks: Verify exact cause of death and governing regulation.; Identify claim type and eligible dependants.; Obtain medical/inquiry record through authorised channel.; Refer attribution questions to designated authority.
Records: Death certificate; inquiry findings; service records; family documents
Risks: Never deny all family pension because of suicide; Avoid conclusory causation without evidence

title: Death while pensioner: starting family pension
body:
Question: A veteran receiving SPARSH pension dies. What can next of kin do?
Legal position: CGDA identifies a sequence of reporting death as an event and initiating family pension, attaching appropriate certificates. Eligibility remains a matter of the sanction and approved family records.
Checks: Report death promptly through authorised SPARSH channel.; Upload death certificate and update contact details.; Initiate family pension claim after event approval.; Track the service request and resolve mismatches.
Records: Death certificate; PPO; family claimant ID; bank information; marriage/dependancy proof
Risks: Do not use deceased pensioner credentials improperly; Do not treat portal acceptance as entitlement approval
references: V6-S12|Death reporting, Initiate Family Pension | V6-S01|regs 62-80

title: Cadet training casualty
body:
Question: Do cadets fall under exactly the same pension rules as soldiers?
Legal position: DESW FAQ identifies separately described ex gratia provisions for cadets who suffer training-attributable disablement or death. Eligibility and rates must be checked against specific cadet rules and current modifications.
Checks: Establish cadet category and training incident date.; Document causal connection and medical board.; Obtain cadet-specific sanction.; Refer to competent service and pension authority.
Records: Cadet enrolment; training programme; injury report; medical assessment; family proof
Risks: Do not apply regular officer thresholds to cadet awards; Avoid quoting rates from 2008 without revision

title: OROP: 2024 tables and 2025 correction
body:
Question: Can an app compute OROP without the latest corrected table?
Legal position: DESW lists OROP revision w.e.f. 1 July 2024 and a correction issued 13 October 2025 to tables 11,26,48,59,94. A rate engine must load both the base tables and corrigendum by provenance, rank, group and qualifying service.
Checks: Identify pensioner class, rank, group, qualifying service and retirement date.; Load authorised base 2024 table and corrected entries from 2025.; Determine applicable row/column with exclusions.; Compare PPO and explain difference with cited cells.
Records: PPO; OROP table IDs; retirement service record; correction letter
Risks: No rates from a remembered table; Avoid treating all ranks as having same retirement terms

title: Commutation and restoration
body:
Question: A pensioner disputes a commutation deduction. Where are the records?
Legal position: Commuted value, deduction and restoration depend on sanctioned commutation and pension-payment records. CGDA FAQ directs users to SPARSH pension slip, entitlement view and PPO. Actual restoration rules must be checked under applicable scheme.
Checks: Retrieve PPO and payment history.; Check commutation sanction date and amount.; Verify restoration due date by applicable order.; Raise a documented correction if system differs.
Records: Commutation order; PPO; SPARSH pension slips; payment ledger
Risks: Do not claim the restoration period is universally identical; Do not assume a missing payment automatically reflects wrong entitlement

title: SPARSH PPO and entitlements
body:
Question: Where should pensioner verify current sanctioned award?
Legal position: SPARSH provides PPO, entitlement details and monthly pension slips, according to CGDA. A payment slip records disbursement; a PPO reflects sanctioned entitlement; conflicts require reconciliation with governing legal authority.
Checks: Obtain login through approved mechanism.; Download PPO and last three slips.; Compare entitlements, arrears, deductions and commutation.; Raise grievance against correct deficiency type.
Records: PPO; monthly slips; entitlements page; bank credit
Risks: Do not store credentials in legal assistant; No unauthorised access to pensioner medical or bank records

title: Life certificate and annual identification
body:
Question: Pension stopped for failure to submit life certificate: what should be done?
Legal position: CGDA FAQ describes digital and manual life certificate processes. This is a disbursement compliance issue, not necessarily loss of underlying entitlement; verify status before advising litigation.
Checks: Verify identification due date and current status.; Use authorised digital/manual method.; Retain acknowledgement and seek restoration/arrears where due.; Escalate service centre support if unable to authenticate.
Records: Acknowledgement; MLC/DLC receipt; PPO; payment history
Risks: Avoid treating payment suspension as forfeiture of pension; No passwords or biometrics in third-party knowledge base

title: Underpayment, unsanctioned component and grievance
body:
Question: PPO shows wrong entitlement or pension slip shows wrong amount: where to complain?
Legal position: CGDA distinguishes payment-related discrepancies from elements not sanctioned in the PPO. Selecting the wrong grievance category may delay resolution.
Checks: Identify whether sanction or disbursement is wrong.; Compare PPO and monthly slip by component.; Attach legal reference, chronology and prior requests.; Route sanction issue to competent pension authority and payment issue through SPARSH as appropriate.
Records: PPO; slips; supporting sanction; grievance acknowledgement
Risks: No direct modification of PPO from chatbot; Do not raise repetitive unsupported claims

title: Constant Attendant Allowance
body:
Question: Is CAA available for severe impairment?
Legal position: PRA and later Government orders provide for constant attendance allowance in specified cases. DESW lists a 30 April 2025 CAA enhancement letter. Actual current rate and medical eligibility must be verified before a calculation.
Checks: Check whether medical criteria and award category are met.; Identify current amount/effective date in 2025 order.; Review sanction and SPARSH PPO.; Use correct unsanctioned-element grievance if required.
Records: Medical/attendance recommendation; PPO; CAA order; payment history
Risks: Do not quote an outdated amount; CAA not automatic for every disabled pensioner
references: V6-S01|reg 89 | V6-S09|CAA enhancement 30 April 2025 | V6-S12|CAA FAQ

title: ECHS and medical benefits
body:
Question: Does a pensioner automatically receive all ECHS facilities?
Legal position: PRA 2008 mentions ECHS and exceptions, but current ECHS eligibility, membership and contribution guidance may differ by cohort, service and scheme. Treat medical benefit as an independently checked entitlement.
Checks: Check pensioner category and ECHS current policy.; Confirm membership/card and dependant eligibility.; Locate exceptions for special classes.; Escalate treatment/empanelment issue through appropriate ECHS channel.
Records: PPO; ECHS card; service category; contribution proof
Risks: PRA 2008 rates/allowances are historical; Do not give clinical treatment recommendations as legal conclusions

title: Tax treatment and deductions
body:
Question: Can the assistant assert every disability payment is income-tax exempt?
Legal position: Tax treatment depends on current law, circulars, litigation and exact pension category. The 2023 MoD press note explicitly described some tax issues as sub judice. The safe response is source-based issue-spotting, not categorical tax advice.
Checks: Identify exact component and award category.; Check current CBDT/tax statute and pending litigation.; Separate SPARSH TDS from legal tax liability.; Refer complex tax position to qualified tax adviser/finance authority.
Records: PPO; Form 16; tax communication; legal status of any circular
Risks: Do not automatically exempt all impairment relief; Do not use old exemption circular without checking judicial status
references: V6-S06|para 39 | V6-S12|Tax summary and TDS FAQs

title: Disability presumption in historical cases
body:
Question: Is no recorded disease at enlistment enough to obtain disability pension?
Legal position: Dharamvir Singh and Rajbir Singh discuss presumptions under the earlier entitlement-rule regime. N S Yadav (2019) warns against automatic attribution of mental illness when relevant facts and medical evidence do not support nexus.
Checks: Identify rule version and date of illness/discharge.; Read actual medical board reasoning, not only percentage.; Compare precedents on close facts.; Check any later Supreme Court treatment.
Records: Enrolment medical; service stress/duty history; board opinion; judgments
Risks: Do not announce a blanket presumption for all 2023 claims; Do not rely on one favourable quotation while omitting limiting precedent
references: V6-S14|2013 | V6-S15|2015 case citation verify | V6-S16|2019 paras 15-19

title: Broad-banding and completion-of-tenure retirees
body:
Question: Do Ram Avtar principles apply to all disability pension applicants?
Legal position: Ram Avtar addressed eligible personnel leaving after completion of tenure with disability attributable/aggravated by service. It does not establish entitlement when disability is not accepted or an entirely different scheme applies.
Checks: Establish accepted service nexus.; Classify mode of discharge and scheme.; Read 2014 order and implementing government circulars.; Compute only after accepted award and source date are clear.
Records: Medical entitlement; retirement order; PPO; broad-banding implementing letter
Risks: No entitlement without service nexus; Do not overread arrears claim from broad-banding eligibility
references: V6-S17|2014 Ram Avtar | V6-S18|2026 Feb paras 12-14

title: February and October 2026 Girish Kumar decisions
body:
Question: Are full historic arrears payable in every pension claim after the February judgment?
Legal position: NO. The 12 February 2026 decision concerned eligible ex-servicemen already receiving disability pension who sought recomputation through broad-banding. The Supreme Court clarified on 12 October 2026 that it cannot be read as granting disability pension and arrears in every case; each claim is decided on its own merits.
Checks: Classify current matter as entitlement dispute or recalculation of existing award.; Compare facts to 2026 INSC 149 and October clarification 2026 INSC 1113.; Analyse delay/limitation and finality separately.; Seek legal advice before demanding universal arrears.
Records: Existing PPO; claim/appeal dates; prior final orders; two 2026 decisions
Risks: Never show February decision without October clarification; Pending later judgment may change interpretation
Example: A veteran already paid disability pension seeks broad-banding recalculation. A different veteran seeks first entitlement to disability pension: those cases must not be treated as identical.

title: Pension rights and executive circulars
body:
Question: Can an executive policy letter remove a clear regulatory concession?
Legal position: Balakrishnan Mullikote (2026 INSC 286) held, in a DSC condonation context, that executive letters cannot override the clear text of applicable pension regulations. It does not eliminate the need to identify which regulation applies.
Checks: Locate regulation and operative policy letter.; Identify any inconsistency.; Study the judgment’s exact scope, especially DSC facts.; Seek legal determination; do not unilaterally disregard an order.
Records: Regulation provision; restrictive circular; rejection order; service record
Risks: Do not generalise a DSC entitlement to all schemes; Do not override an official sanction without competence

title: Two appeals versus AFT application
body:
Question: Which forum should receive a disability entitlement challenge?
Legal position: Pension entitlement schemes may provide internal first/second appeals and the Armed Forces Tribunal Act regulates judicial remedies and limitation. The two clocks are not identical; medical appeal dates cannot substitute for AFT limitation analysis.
Checks: Identify date rejection was communicated.; Read applicable entitlement-rule appeal process and any revisions.; Record first and second appeal status.; Separately analyse AFT Act ss 14,21,22 and forum exceptions.
Records: Rejection communication; appeal papers; dates and acknowledgements; AFT rules
Risks: Do not assume filing an appeal indefinitely extends all deadlines; Do not state that all pension matters are within AFT jurisdiction without checking statutory exclusions
references: V6-S07|Chapter I para 5 | V6-S21|ss 14,21,22 | V6-S08|historic appeals

title: Pension arrears and limitation
body:
Question: Does a recurring pension wrong automatically defeat any limitation defence?
Legal position: Pension may create recurring effects, but claim type, earlier finality, applicable policy and judicial precedent control arrears. The October 2026 Girish Kumar clarification squarely rejects universalisation of the February ruling.
Checks: Distinguish initial claim, revision, wrongful cessation and arrears only.; Capture challenge dates and final orders.; Identify pension category and factual analogy.; Obtain AFT/court legal opinion before calculating back-payment.
Records: Demand and rejection letters; PPO revision history; court orders; chronology
Risks: Avoid blanket three-year arrears rule or blanket unlimited-arrears rule; Do not ignore 2026 clarification

title: Source integrity for future offline legal assistant
body:
Question: How can an offline assistant be prevented from inventing pension entitlements?
Legal position: Every output must retrieve versioned original authority, identify application dates, map relevant facts and expose uncertainties. Policy rates and court treatment need update controls before outputs can be actioned.
Checks: Require service category + rank + key dates.; Only cite stored source_id and provision locator.; Block amount calculation unless approved table rows exist.; Show conflicts and later-treatment warnings prominently.; Maintain review signature and timestamp.
Records: SHA-256 original source; approved knowledge record; change log; source-to-answer trace
Risks: Do not upload personal medical/pension data to public AI tools; Do not treat editorial notes as delegated legal authority
references: V6-S03|source portal | V6-S09|circular register | V6-S19|later treatment

body:
