Later treatment / limitation: Do not generalise DSC factual holding to all pension matters.

title: Identify the correct forum
body: A soldier seeks relief after an adverse service order: where should the case begin? Under s14, AFT is the specialised first-instance adjudicatory forum for defined service matters. A statutory appeal from a court-martial arises under s15. Constitutional review by a High Court remains available under Art 226, but this does not make a writ a substitute for the ordinary forum in every case.  Assessment: Record whether challenge is to service order, court-martial or pure constitutional issue; Read s3(o) inclusion/exclusion and s2 personnel applicability; Match remedy to s14 or s15; Test s21 remedy exhaustion, s22 time issues and territorial Bench; Refer jurisdiction doubt to JAG before filing  Documentation: Impugned order; Service status and rank proof; Petition/reply trail; Complete case chronology  Risks: Blindly directing every grievance to AFT; Filing an OA instead of court-martial appeal; Assuming Art 226 always creates original forum of choice  Example: An officer challenging a non-selection order generally raises service-matter issues; a petition against a GCM conviction engages s15.

title: Test status of applicant and successors
body: Can a widow or retired person pursue an AFT service claim? Section 2(2) extends applicability to retired personnel, including dependants, heirs and successors insofar as their service matters are concerned. Entitlement to the particular relief and authority to represent an estate remain separate questions.  Assessment: Identify original servicemember and statutory service status; Establish death, retirement or discharge dates; Verify relationship, succession or nomination documents; Confirm claimed benefit relates to qualifying service matter; Check any necessary parties and records  Documentation: Service record; Death certificate if relevant; Nomination or legal-heir proof; Pension order; Impugned refusal  Risks: Presuming family relationship proves entitlement; Ignoring other beneficiaries or necessary parties; Treating service eligibility and pension merits as identical  Example: A spouse seeking family pension should identify the underlying service record and applicable entitlement rules before drafting relief.

title: Identify exclusions in service matters
body: Does every complaint about posting, leave or summary punishment reach AFT? Section 3(o) lists remuneration, pension, tenure and related subjects, while excluding certain Presidential pleasure orders, transfers/postings, leave and a stated category of SCM matters. Read the exact exclusion and distinguish any separate claim under s15.  Assessment: Break combined grievance into legally distinct claims; Test each against s3(o)(i)-(iv) exclusions; Determine whether s15 court-martial appeal may independently apply; Research binding decisions in territorial jurisdiction; Record reason for accepting or denying jurisdiction  Documentation: Exact administrative order; Relief requested; Jurisdiction note; Relevant bench precedent  Risks: Treating broad any other matter language as unrestricted; Conflating transfer with promotion; Assuming excluded s14 SCM case necessarily outside s15  Example: Posting challenge and seniority claim in one application require issue-wise forum screening.

title: Section 14 original application versus section 15 court-martial appeal
body: Which statutory route applies after court-martial? Section 14 governs service-matter applications. Section 15 provides appellate jurisdiction over an order, decision, finding or sentence passed by court-martial, with specified powers over conviction, sentence and bail. Do not force a trial appeal into a generic service-law cause of action.  Assessment: Identify tribunal order sought; Obtain complete trial record, confirmation and post-trial petitions; Locate applicable court-martial appeal rules and limitations; Plead errors of law, evidence or miscarriage of justice precisely; Identify relief within s15(4)-(6)  Documentation: Charge sheet; Proceedings and exhibits; Findings/sentence; Confirmation and promulgation; Petitions and orders  Risks: Only asserting natural justice without identifying the trial defect; Mistaking merits review for de novo trial; Failing to consider s15 appellate power to enhance after hearing  Example: A soldier dismissed by a SCM must receive a distinct jurisdiction analysis under ss3(o),14 and 15.

title: Summary Court-Martial route: a litigation-sensitive issue
body: Does a short SCM sentence automatically remove the AFT as possible forum? The wording of s3(o)(iv) excludes SCM from the service-matter definition except for dismissal or imprisonment exceeding three months; however courts have analysed whether s15 independently admits appeals from SCM findings. This issue must be treated as an authority-sensitive interpretation and escalated.  Assessment: Capture SCM type and exact punishment; Decide whether grievance attacks sentence, conviction, discharge or service consequences; Compare s3(o) with s15(1)-(2); Read Nk Santosh Lohar and subsequent binding rulings; Refer contested forum route to JAG and counsel  Documentation: Original SCM order; Punishment quantum; Trial record; Current controlling precedent  Risks: Flat claim no SCM appeal lies; Misreading a High Court view as uniformly binding across India; Converting litigation uncertainty into a mandatory rule  Example: SCM with 30 days detention is not automatically answered solely by the literal service-matter exclusion.

title: Territorial Bench and ordinary residence option
body: Where should a retired pensioner file? The 2008 Procedure Rules, Rule 6, relate Bench selection to current or last posting, or place of cause of action; a person who has ceased to be in service can, at option, use the Bench of ordinary residence. Local Bench notifications and current roster must be checked.  Assessment: Verify current service/retired status; Identify last posting and cause of action locations; For retired claimant document ordinary residence; Confirm notified Bench jurisdiction and present filing mode; Record reasons when more than one candidate Bench exists  Documentation: Last posting order; Residential proof; Cause of action record; Jurisdictional Bench notification  Risks: Treating convenient filing place as automatic entitlement; Assuming a Bench sits permanently at every notified city; Overlooking transferred-case powers under s27  Example: A veteran ordinarily residing in Telangana may have a residence-based option even if last served in another state.

title: Necessary and proper parties
body: Who must be named as respondent? A proper party array should identify the authority responsible for the impugned decision, the Union or competent government department where necessary, and anyone whose accrued rights may be materially affected. The correct list depends on the impugned order and the applicable tribunal rules.  Assessment: Trace impugned order to decision-maker; Identify implementing and record-holding authorities; Consider directly affected third parties; Align relief against each respondent; Verify current name/address and service particulars  Documentation: Order chain; Respondent directory; Selection or promotion list if relevant; Official addresses  Risks: Omitting decision-maker; Seeking adverse relief against unrepresented third party; Unnecessary large respondent array  Example: Promotion re-fixation affecting another officer may require careful examination of third-party hearing rights.

title: Combined grievances and multiple causes
body: Can a petitioner combine a discharge dispute, pension claim and separate promotion grievance? The 2008 Procedure Rules, Rule 10, contemplate a single cause of action while permitting consequential relief. Distinct events and unrelated causes should not be mechanically combined merely because they concern the same service member.  Assessment: List each impugned order with date; Group rights arising from one transaction; Separate independent causes and limitation calculations; Identify consequential versus freestanding reliefs; Confirm case pleading structure with counsel  Documentation: Chronology; Impugned orders; Relief matrix; Separate cause-of-action note  Risks: Omnibus OA obscuring jurisdiction; Adding unrelated respondents; Using later event to renew time for older cause  Example: Consequential restoration of pension after an unlawful discharge may relate to the same cause, while an unrelated earlier promotion claim may not.

title: Exhaustion of statutory remedies
body: Can an officer file an OA immediately after a grievance arises? Section 21(1) requires the AFT ordinarily to be satisfied that remedies available under the relevant Service Act, rules and regulations have been availed. The statute allows deemed exhaustion upon final rejection or six months without final order on qualifying representation.  Assessment: Find specific statutory petition or complaint procedure; Identify competent authority and submission date; Preserve service/postal acknowledgement; Identify final decision or six-month non-disposal date; Assess any urgent exception with counsel  Documentation: Statutory complaint; Transmission receipt; Reminder record; Final reply; Applicable grievance regulation  Risks: Using an informal email as presumed statutory petition; Treating six months as a general delay extension; Filing before checking correct authority  Example: No reply after six months may permit deemed exhaustion, but does not automatically establish merits or eliminate all limitation concerns.

title: Final rejection and time calculation
body: What clock runs after rejection of a statutory complaint? Section 22(1)(a) generally links filing to six months from the final rejection under s21(2)(a), with power under s22(2) to admit later filing on sufficient cause. Exact trigger date, service/receipt and applicable exceptions must be documented.  Assessment: Identify actual final order and competent issuer; Preserve dispatch, communication and receipt dates separately; Calculate filing position with conservative earliest-date assumption; Determine need for affidavit-backed condonation; Record legal reasoning and current interpretations  Documentation: Final rejection copy; Posting and delivery proof; Limitation worksheet; Condonation supporting affidavit  Risks: Counting from representation rather than final order; Ignoring uncertainty over communication; Inferring automatic extension from reminders  Example: A complaint rejected in writing should generate a dated limitation assessment immediately on receipt.

title: Unanswered petition and statutory text issue
body: What does the six-month silence rule mean for filing time? Section 21(2)(b) deals with deemed exhaustion after a six-month non-disposal period. Section 22(1)(b) refers to the unanswered-representation case, but publicly reproduced text does not express a complete independent filing formula as clearly as clause (a). Avoid automatic calculation until current authoritative text and case-law treatment are checked.  Assessment: Record petition receipt date; Identify six-month non-disposal date; Preserve all interim communications; Verify current authenticated text of s22(1)(b); Refer limitation date to JAG, do not use a hard-coded last day  Documentation: Stamped representation; Delivery evidence; Follow-up record; Legal limitation note  Risks: Hard-coding s22(1)(b) from inference; Equating deemed exhaustion with no limitation; Treating a reminder as resetting cause of action  Example: Application should display REVIEW REQUIRED for a non-response case, with the six-month exhaustion date shown but not an asserted filing deadline.

title: Condonation of delay
body: May an AFT admit a late OA? Section 22(2) gives power to admit qualifying delayed applications if sufficient cause is shown. Procedure Rule 8(9) calls for a separate affidavit-backed application for condonation. Grant is discretionary and must not be promised.  Assessment: Compute and disclose period of delay; Explain whole interval with supporting facts; Separate legal excuse from merits; Attach affidavit and proof of circumstances; Seek order on condonation before assuming admissibility  Documentation: Limitation chart; Condonation application; Affidavit; Medical/communication/proceeding documents  Risks: Saying delay automatically condoned because pension is recurring; Unexplained long periods; Concealing prior litigation  Example: Three years of unexplained inaction after final rejection needs a fact-specific condonation application, not a generic sentence.

title: Continuing wrong and recurring pension shortfall
body: Does monthly underpayment restart limitation for all arrears? Tarsem Singh distinguishes a continuing wrong from stale claims and cautions against prejudice to settled third-party rights. Arrears may be limited despite a current grievance; the decision must be applied with statutory limitation rules and facts.  Assessment: Separate entitlement declaration from money arrears; Identify whether error continues monthly; Identify date of first denial and later rejections; Consider third-party rights (seniority/promotion); Research applicable arrears periods and delay doctrine  Documentation: PPO; Monthly payment record; Original refusal; Representation history; Applicable pension instructions  Risks: Claiming unlimited historic arrears; Treating stale promotion as continuing wrong; Using Tarsem Singh as substitute for s22  Example: An incorrect recurring pension component may merit current relief but not necessarily payment for decades of arrears.

title: Multiple representations and limitation
body: Do repeated reminders revive an old cause? Repetitive representations generally do not themselves create a fresh adverse order or revive a concluded cause. Examine whether the authority issued a genuinely new independent decision or simply reiterated the earlier rejection.  Assessment: Locate first operative adverse order; Compare later communications to that order; Identify any statutory reconsideration right; Prepare earliest defensible limitation calculation; Seek specific opinion where later policy creates new entitlement  Documentation: First and subsequent replies; Original petition; Authority/circular triggering later reassessment  Risks: Limitation shopping through reminders; Treating every RTI response as new order; Ignoring a genuine later policy cause  Example: A 2026 reminder about a 2018 promotion denial normally needs more than its dispatch date to establish fresh cause.

title: Pre-existing and transferred litigation
body: What if proceedings were pending when AFT was created? Sections 34 and 35 address transition and transfer of pending cases and specified historic appeal situations. These provisions are not a general fresh extension for ordinary current applications.  Assessment: Identify original court and filing date; Ascertain whether statutory transfer occurred; Obtain docket and transfer orders; Avoid duplicate proceedings; Seek JAG/counsel review of procedural continuity  Documentation: Original case filing; Transfer order; AFT assigned number; Pleading record  Risks: Parallel litigation in old forum and AFT; Using historical transitory rules for new cases  Example: A transferred High Court case must carry its earlier pleadings and orders into the current record.

title: OA factual chronology
body: What must precede drafting an Original Application? The factual spine of a good OA is an ordered chronology identifying events, disputed decisions, service remedies and requested relief. Rule 4 contemplates an index and list of relevant dates, while Rule 8 requires numbered readable pleading paragraphs.  Assessment: Build date-verified event table; Separate admitted facts from disputed assertions; Identify rule in force on each event date; Attach primary documents in sequence; Link every requested relief to pleaded fact and legal ground  Documentation: Date-event chart; Source record log; Orders and representations; Annexure index  Risks: Contradictory dates; Unsupported procedural allegations; Omitting unfavourable records  Example: Promotion petition should show eligibility date, board date, policy date, representation and decision, not a narrative without source anchors.

title: Original Application pleading architecture
body: What sections should an OA contain? A well-structured OA normally includes parties, jurisdiction, limitation and remedy exhaustion, facts, legal grounds, reliefs, interim relief if any, verification/affidavit and annexures. Actual Registry format and Form I control; the template in this package is illustrative only.  Assessment: Verify correct Bench and Form I; State applicable provision and maintainability; Plead facts chronologically in numbered paragraphs; Identify distinct grounds and precise prayers; Complete verification, supporting affidavit and service  Documentation: Final OA; Form I; Index; List of dates; Order; Annexures; Vakalatnama when applicable  Risks: Copying another case without facts; Praying vague justice; Mixing legal conclusions into chronology  Example: Ask for quashing of identified order and well-defined consequential relief, not a general direction to redress grievance.

title: Registry filing and technical scrutiny
body: What happens after papers reach AFT Registry? Rules 4–5 concern filing, receipt endorsement, scrutiny and rectification of defects. The Registrar may return substantially defective papers and the Rules identify an avenue for challenge to a Registry refusal. Check current electronic or physical filing practice.  Assessment: File signed indexed sets in current accepted mode; Obtain stamped or electronic acknowledgement; Record diary and registration numbers; Correct objections within authorised time; Preserve proof of revised filing date  Documentation: Filing acknowledgement; Defect memo; Corrected sets; Registry correspondence  Risks: Assuming postal dispatch equals registration; Ignoring defect-memo deadlines; Applying old triplicate protocol to a different current e-filing directive without checking  Example: A registry objection about missing annexure must be tracked like a legal deadline.

title: Affidavits and verification
body: Which pleadings require a supporting affidavit? The 2011 amendment inserted Rule 12A requiring applications under Rule 8 and replies under Rule 12 to be affidavit-supported. Verification must be by an authorised person with actual knowledge or accurately identified record knowledge.  Assessment: Identify deponent and source of personal knowledge; Separate statements on personal knowledge from record-based belief; Check authority to swear for government respondent; Match annexures and paragraph references; Execute attestation before proper person  Documentation: Affidavit; Authorisation; Verified copies; Deponent source records  Risks: Deponent swearing facts beyond knowledge; Missing 2011 amendment; Unsigned corrections  Example: A Records Officer cannot swear as an eyewitness to a 15-year-old accident unless he distinguishes documentary knowledge.

title: Filing fees and 2011 amendment
body: Does every AFT OA attract the original Rule 7 fee? The 2008 Rule 7 initially provided a general application-fee scheme. The 2011 amendment restricts the circumstances in which that specified fee is payable. Use the amended category text and current Bench instructions, not the old unamended paragraph alone.  Assessment: Identify OA, RA, CA, restoration or transfer request category; Read gazetted 2011 amendment and subsequent changes; Confirm current acceptable payment mode and exemption policy; Preserve payment proof if payable  Documentation: Application type; Latest fee instruction; Receipt or exemption order  Risks: Charging ₹250 automatically for all OAs; Using outdated method of demand draft without Registry check; Inventing exemption  Example: The app should not show a mandatory OA fee until it has tested the amended Rule 7 categories.

title: Annexure integrity and pagination
body: How should records be assembled for litigation? Rule 9 requires attested copies of the impugned order, relied-upon documents and an index, with serialised annexures. Reliable litigation also requires legible copies, correct chronology, retention of original records and protection of classified material.  Assessment: Assign annexure numbers and stable document IDs; Preserve original signed documents separately; Validate date/page/paragraph references; Redact only under authorised directions; Capture controlled custody and hash metadata for digital files  Documentation: Annexure index; Document originals; Hash manifest; Classified-material handling approvals  Risks: Unapproved disclosure of classified information; Altered copies without audit trail; Incomplete medical or promotion records  Example: For medical-board litigation, annex original board decision and authentic service documents without changing diagnosis wording.

title: Counter-affidavit and factual reply
body: How should a respondent headquarters reply to an OA? Procedure Rule 12 requires the respondent to admit, deny or explain material allegations specifically and provide relevant documents; Rule 12A requires affidavit support. An effective reply grounds every contention in a cited contemporaneous record.  Assessment: Open issue-by-issue paragraph matrix; Identify officer competent to make affidavit; Collect complete primary records and exact policy edition; Answer each allegation distinctly; State preliminary objections and merits separately; Obtain legal and command approval before filing  Documentation: OA copy; Para-wise reply matrix; Signed records; Source policy; Deponent authorisation  Risks: Mechanical blanket denial; Suppressing adverse records; Unsupported security/privilege claims; Missing authorisation  Example: If a soldier alleges an unfair inquiry, deny only facts actually contradicted by convening order, proceedings and signed opportunities.

title: Rejoinder and additional pleading
body: May parties introduce new facts after the reply? A rejoinder should ordinarily address new matters in the respondent reply; independent new grounds or causes require procedural permission or amendment as appropriate. Follow Tribunal directions and Practice Rules rather than treating rejoinder as an unlimited second OA.  Assessment: Compare reply with OA; Identify genuinely new facts; Support responses with records; Seek leave for additional pleadings when required; Protect hearing schedule and opposing party notice  Documentation: OA and reply; Proposed rejoinder; Leave order if applicable; Additional annexures  Risks: Completely changing the case via rejoinder; Late surprise documents; Unsigned additional affidavits  Example: New record disclosed by Union in its reply can be addressed in rejoinder with proper permission.
references: V7-S02|Rules 12-13; V7-S04|Practice Rules on pleadings and amendments

title: Representation through counsel and authorisation
body: Who may appear for a servicemember or the Union? Section 25 allows an applicant/appellant to appear personally or through chosen legal practitioner. The government may authorise legal practitioners or law officers; formal authorisation and valid vakalatnama/representation documents must be filed where required.  Assessment: Verify whether party appears in person or through counsel; For government, obtain standing-counsel/law-officer authorisation; Confirm signing authority and current counsel record; File valid vakalatnama or authorisation; Coordinate instructions through authorised legal chain  Documentation: Vakalatnama; Government counsel authorisation; Affidavit authority; Case handover notes  Risks: Unlicensed representation; Assuming every unit officer can argue for the Union; Sending legal instructions through unauthorised channel  Example: The CO may provide case records and factual instructions, but should not treat that as a personal mandate to conduct government litigation.

title: Confidential and classified service records
body: How should sensitive Army documents be handled in proceedings? The Tribunal has production powers under s14(4), subject to statutory qualifications, and can regulate in-camera proceedings under s23. A unit should preserve evidence while applying authorised classification, privilege and controlled-disclosure procedures.  Assessment: Identify document classification and custody; Route disclosure request to competent authority/counsel; Preserve full original; Propose authenticated non-sensitive extracts where legally permissible; Seek Tribunal protective or in-camera directions when justified  Documentation: Document classification log; Government privilege decision; Disclosure order; Redaction approval  Risks: Unilateral deletion of relevant material; Publishing confidential records in open pleadings; Blanket unreasoned national security claim  Example: Confidential report records need an authorised evidence-management process, not casual attachment to email.

title: Interim relief under section 26
body: Can the Tribunal stay a retirement or discharge order urgently? Section 26 ordinarily requires supply of interim application/documents and opportunity to be heard; an exceptional ex parte order requires reasons. The section also establishes a 14-day disposal mechanism for specified applications to vacate such an order, with automatic-vacation consequence in described circumstances.  Assessment: Identify imminent irreparable consequence and date; Disclose all material facts and prior proceedings; Serve proposed documents unless exceptional procedure invoked; Draft narrowly tailored interim prayer; Track stay, variation and vacation proceedings continuously  Documentation: Impugned order; Urgency chronology; Proof of service; Interim order copy; Vacation application  Risks: Assuming every stay is ex parte; Omitting section 26(2) deadline consequences; Continuing action despite served stay  Example: If retirement is due in two days, describe exact consequences and what preservation order is sought rather than ask for general stay of all proceedings.

title: Documents, affidavits and oral evidence
body: Is AFT a full civil trial with automatic oral testimony? Section 23 states AFT is not bound by CPC procedure and is guided by natural justice; it decides ordinarily on records, affidavits and argument, while oral evidence may be allowed on recorded reasons. Section 14(4) confers specified civil-court-like powers.  Assessment: Identify disputed material fact; File reliable documents and affidavits; Explain why oral evidence or production is necessary; Seek narrowly identified record directions; Preserve witness availability and service  Documentation: Paper book; Affidavits; Material-fact statement; Document-production application  Risks: Promising automatic witness examination; Seeking fishing discovery; Treating every factual disagreement as basis for trial  Example: A disputed signature may require specific proof; the AFT can decide whether oral evidence is necessary.

title: Judicial review standard in service disputes
body: Will a Tribunal replace a selection board’s assessment? Judicial review ordinarily tests authority, procedure, reasonableness, discrimination and legal error rather than substituting the Tribunal as promotion board or command authority. The applicable service policy and controlling judgments decide the standard in each subject.  Assessment: Identify precise illegality asserted; Obtain complete policy effective on decision date; Show record contradiction or procedural breach; Distinguish merits disagreement from legal infirmity; Frame relief within statutory jurisdiction  Documentation: Selection policy; Board record; Comparative material where legally available; Impugned decision  Risks: Seeking de novo selection by judge; Withholding applicable policy; Unsupported allegation of bias  Example: An officer cannot establish unlawful non-selection merely by claiming better achievements than selected peers.

title: Grounds of court-martial appellate intervention
body: What must a court-martial appeal plead? Section 15(4) expressly includes legally unsustainable finding, wrong decision on question of law, and material irregularity causing miscarriage of justice. The power to mitigate, commute or enhance sentence is governed by s15(6) and due hearing requirements.  Assessment: Build trial error chart by charge and finding; Link each ground to exact record page; Explain effect on justice outcome; Separate conviction and sentencing grounds; Request legally available relief and avoid unsupported innocence declaration  Documentation: Certified trial proceedings; Evidence/exhibits; Rule compliance notes; Findings and confirmation; Post-trial petitions  Risks: Relying on technical defects without miscarriage analysis; Ignoring lawful substitution or enhancement powers; Missing material documents  Example: Record that a witness was denied without lawful basis and explain why testimony mattered, not only the denial.

title: Bail and sentence pending appeal
body: Can AFT grant bail or suspend sentence? Section 15(3) confers bail power with an express death/life-imprisonment exception; s15(6) permits specified parole/suspension and sentence orders. These are judicial powers to be sought on case-specific grounds, not automatic consequences of filing an appeal.  Assessment: Check status as accused/appellant and military custody; Identify offence, sentence and statutory restriction; Prepare relevant facts and conduct record; Define exact relief and conditions; Implement only on receipt of operative judicial order  Documentation: Custody warrant; Sentence; Appeal grounds; Medical or family urgency evidence; Judicial order  Risks: Promising release by filing appeal; Acting on oral informal assurance; Ignoring special bail limitations  Example: A request to suspend a custodial sentence must identify proper statutory subsection and case facts.

title: Case orders and compliance tracking
body: What must a unit do on receiving an AFT interim or final order? A judicial order must be read precisely for operative directions, parties, deadlines, conditions and any stay. Section 29 requires execution of Tribunal orders. A unit should immediately route instructions to the competent authority and counsel and preserve proof of action.  Assessment: Authenticate signed order; Extract operative directions and calculation dates; Identify responsible authority, not just unit custodian; Freeze action inconsistent with stay; Submit compliance evidence and report obstacles promptly  Documentation: Certified/order portal copy; Legal cell acknowledgement; Compliance sheet; Payment/service entries; Appeal/stay instructions  Risks: Assuming appeal automatically stays an order; Missing time-bound implementation; Altering legal effect by paraphrase  Example: If AFT directs reconsideration rather than direct promotion, implement reconsideration through competent board, not a direct rank grant by unit.

title: Review application within AFT
body: What if a clear error appears in the AFT order? Section 14(4)(f) recognises review power; Rule 18 of the 2008 Procedure Rules specifies a 30-day period from receipt of the copy for filing a review application. Review is not an unrestricted second appeal; identify a legally recognised ground.  Assessment: Obtain authenticated order and date of receipt; Identify apparent error or permitted review ground; Check whether review or appeal is suitable; Prepare affidavit and applicable fee category; File within current rule deadline or obtain specific advice on any delay  Documentation: Order copy and receipt; Error matrix; Review pleading; Affidavit; Fee confirmation  Risks: Review to reargue losing case; Missing 30-day issue; Assuming review automatically stops Supreme Court deadline  Example: A mistaken arithmetic entry in the operative direction might support review; disagreement with evidence appreciation ordinarily requires different analysis.

title: Appeal to Supreme Court: statutory route
body: Does every AFT loser have an appeal as of right? Sections 30–31 prescribe the Supreme Court appeal route. A final order other than contempt order is subject to statutory leave and a substantial public-law threshold; interlocutory appeals are excluded under s30(1). Separate conditions apply to contempt decisions under s30(2).  Assessment: Classify final, interlocutory or contempt order; Identify point of law of general public importance or ground for SC leave; Note 90-day and 30-day statutory periods as relevant; Document legal opinion and approval for government appeal; Preserve order communication dates  Documentation: Final AFT judgment; Leave application; Proposed questions of law; Dated receipt proof; Government litigation sanction  Risks: Treating Supreme Court as routine second fact appeal; Ignoring s31 leave; Confusing contempt 60-day route with ordinary 90-day route  Example: A pure disagreement over factual promotion assessment normally does not itself demonstrate a general public-law question.

title: Section 31 leave deadlines
body: What are the two distinct 30-day leave stages? Section 31(2) provides 30 days from AFT decision to seek leave before the Tribunal, and 30 days from refusal to seek leave from the Supreme Court. Section 32 permits the Supreme Court to extend time for appeal and specified SC leave applications; do not assume it authorises AFT to extend every interval.  Assessment: Record judgment date and receipt; Prepare AFT leave application within statutory period; On refusal, capture refusal date; Prepare SC leave/appeal materials immediately; Obtain precise counsel advice on s32 and procedural rules  Documentation: AFT judgment; Leave refusal; Filing diary; Legal opinion; Deadline tracker  Risks: Missing first 30-day stage; Misrepresenting Supreme Court s32 as blanket condonation by all fora; Assuming 90 days means wait to seek leave  Example: The application should maintain two separate deadline entries, not a single 90-day appeal timer.

title: Constitutional route after Parashotam Dass
body: Can a High Court examine an AFT judgment despite s30-31? The 2023 Supreme Court decision confirms Art 226 power of judicial review is not barred by AFT Act architecture. However High Courts retain discretion, self-restraint and ordinary insistence on the specialist forum where appropriate. Earlier Shri Kant Sharma reasoning must be read with later treatment.  Assessment: Identify whether AFT has already ruled; Distinguish legal error, jurisdiction or fundamental-rights complaint; Read Parashotam Dass and later territorial precedent; Assess statutory appeal and constitutional strategy together; Do not bypass ordinary statutory remedies without compelling basis  Documentation: AFT order; Trial or service record; Proposed constitutional grounds; Counsel opinion  Risks: Saying no HC review ever; Saying HC automatically hears every AFT case afresh; Treating Art 136(2) as ordinary armed-forces SLP route  Example: Aft procedural-jurisdiction error may be framed under Art 226, but selection of forum remains case-specific.
references: V7-S07|L Chandra Kumar; V7-S08|Parashotam Dass; V7-S09|historical contrary view; V7-S13|2026 Delhi HC

title: Article 136(2) limitation and confusion
body: Why is an ordinary special leave petition not a simple fallback? Article 136(2) excludes from that Article judgments and orders of any court or tribunal constituted under law relating to the Armed Forces. AFT Act ss30–31 create a distinct route; the interaction with constitutional review is analysed in Parashotam Dass.  Assessment: Identify provenance of order (court-martial or AFT); Read precise Arts 136(2),226 and statutory appeal provisions; Obtain Supreme Court counsel opinion on route; Distinguish Art 226 review from statutory SC leave  Documentation: Order source; Proposed leave questions; Legal route note  Risks: Assuming all military SLPs under Art 136(1) are competent; Ignoring statutory leave restrictions; Confusing AFT orders with High Court writ orders  Example: A court-martial judgment cannot simply be fed into a generic civil SLP filing template.

title: Execution, contempt and post-order remedies
body: What if a favourable AFT order is not implemented? Section 29 deals with execution. Section 19 addresses contempt in the terms stated by that section, and the scope of any contempt relief should not be assumed to match general High Court contempt powers. Implementation should begin with accurate order interpretation and engagement with counsel.  Assessment: Verify service and operative effect of order; Identify compliance deadline and authority; Obtain reasons for non-implementation; Seek execution or other competent remedy through counsel; Preserve all filings, stays and compliance proof  Documentation: Order; Proof of receipt; Department action record; Legal notices; Reply to execution proceedings  Risks: Threatening contempt before reading s19 scope; Claiming every non-compliance automatically criminal contempt; Ignoring valid stay  Example: If an order to revise pension remains unimplemented, first identify Accounts authority and existing stay before selecting legal remedy.

title: Order interpretation and administrative reconsideration
body: Did AFT quash the decision or order a fresh lawful review? Orders granting set-aside, remand, fresh consideration, notional relief or monetary relief have different legal and administrative consequences. Only the exact operative paragraph, read with reasons, determines what the authority must do.  Assessment: Extract operative verbs and time frame; Identify conditions and affected cohort; Allocate actions to legally competent authority; Take contemporaneous legal clarification if ambiguous; Document compliance and communicate reasoned decision  Documentation: Certified judgment; Original decision; Compliance workflow; Fresh order if required  Risks: Treating reconsideration as automatic allowance; Granting relief beyond operative decision; Unrecorded deviation  Example: Direction to reconsider promotion must go back to appropriate authority with lawful criteria, not unilateral CO order.

title: Judgment treatment and precedent checking
body: Can a case digest be cited without checking appeal history? A legal assistant must distinguish binding Supreme Court ratio, territorial High Court decisions, AFT decisions and persuasive commentary. Subsequent appeal, review, stay, overruling, factual distinction or amendments can alter applicability.  Assessment: Search exact party/case number and dates; Fetch original judgment and verify paragraphs; Find later appeal or clarification; Distinguish ratio from dicta and fact-bound finding; Store treatment state as-of date and jurisdiction  Documentation: Certified judgment; Later orders; Citation history; Legal issue classification  Risks: Auto-claiming every AFT decision universally binding; Inserting unverified paragraph numbers; Using a later news summary instead of judgment  Example: A 2015 ruling suggesting a writ bar should not be served without 2023 Parashotam Dass treatment.
references: V7-S07|constitutional hierarchy; V7-S08|example subsequent treatment; V7-S16|judgment portal

title: Immediate response when unit receives legal notice
body: What should a CO do on receiving an AFT notice? Receipt of process triggers record preservation, forwarding and litigation coordination, not unilateral issuance of an ad hoc reply. Rule 11 concerns service and Rule 12 the responsive pleading requirements. Always obey actual Bench directions and authorised legal channels.  Assessment: Date-stamp and log notice; Identify returnable date and standing counsel; Preserve all relevant records and suspend routine destruction; Nominate case officer for factual coordination; Submit para-wise comments through legal channel promptly; Monitor dates and compliance  Documentation: Notice; OA paper book; Unit record index; Transmission receipt; Case officer brief  Risks: Delaying while awaiting next routine file cycle; Destroying originals; Direct communication to petitioner in lieu of reply  Example: A unit receiving a pension OA should secure service, medical and pay records without deciding pension entitlement itself.

title: Evidence preservation and legal hold
body: Which documents must not be destroyed while a case is pending? Pending litigation requires preservation of relevant original and electronic records, including adverse material. This is an editorial litigation-control safeguard; destruction schedules and classified handling are governed by applicable service orders.  Assessment: Issue written preservation notification; Record physical and digital custodians; Collect only authentic originals and forensic copies; Record chain of custody and modification history; Release hold only after legal closure and records-policy approval  Documentation: Preservation order; Record inventory; Checksum manifest; Custodian attestations  Risks: Selective preservation favouring one side; Improper copying of classified files to civilian storage; Deleting emails or CCTV after legal notice  Example: Retain original CoI proceedings and evidence even when no disciplinary action ultimately followed.

title: Para-wise comments from formation to counsel
body: What should factual comments to standing counsel contain? A para-wise comment is an internal source-supported factual brief, not a casual opinion on chances of winning. It should specify admitting/denying facts, documentary support, relevant statutory authorities and disputed facts requiring legal decision.  Assessment: Index each OA paragraph; Mark admitted, denied or explanation; Quote exact document locator, date and custodian; Attach adverse but material evidence; Identify policy version and legal question; Obtain competent approval before forwarding  Documentation: OA; Para-wise comments matrix; Document source register; Competent signature  Risks: Unsubstantiated denial; Reconstructing missing orders; Fabricated retrospective rationales; Omitting service directions  Example: For Rule 180 complaint, provide actual proceedings and opportunity record instead of stating broadly that all rules were followed.

title: Government decision to appeal adverse order
body: Who decides whether to seek leave against AFT? The ability to appeal is statutory, but sanction, competent authority and representation of the Union are governed by applicable government litigation instructions. The unit should provide prompt factual and legal analysis; it does not presume independent authority to institute a Supreme Court appeal.  Assessment: Record judgment and service date immediately; Obtain reasoned legal opinion on arguable question of law; Forward recommendation to competent litigation authority; Track statutory leave periods; Implement order unless a competent court stays operation  Documentation: Order; Legal opinion; Case summary; Financial/service implications; Sanction file  Risks: CO filing government appeal without authority; Treating pending consideration as judicial stay; Missing 30-day leave period  Example: An adverse pension judgment calls for a reasoned appeal proposal, not automatic blanket litigation against retiree.

title: Operational readiness of an offline legal assistant
body: When may the knowledge base answer an AFT case question as authoritative? Only after source authentication, amendment matching, precedent treatment checking and legal approval should the system provide case-specific procedure as operational advice. Until then it should show law excerpts and research notes with conspicuous review status.  Assessment: Capture dates, service status, case stage and exact order type; Retrieve provision and official source version; Search conflicting and later judgments; Show confidence and unanswered legal questions; Escalate jurisdiction, limitation or liberty questions to JAG  Documentation: Source hash; Version-effective metadata; Approved legal note; Judgment treatment graph; Reviewer signature  Risks: LLM inventing case number or deadline; Hidden reliance on expired rules; No audit of quoted legal text  Example: If a query says SCM 45 days detention, app must ask which relief and route, and cite competing interpretations rather than provide one false yes/no answer.
references: V7-S01|Act hierarchy; V7-S03|amendment version; V7-S08|precedent treatment

title: Service grievance to OA
body: AFT Act ss 3(o),14,21-22; Procedure Rules 4-10. Receive order and establish precise cause of action; Review rank/status and whether matter is excluded by s3(o); Identify statutory complaint route and competent authority; Confirm final rejection or six-month deemed exhaustion; Calculate limitation, documenting all relevant dates; Select Bench under Rule 6, assemble Form I and documents; File, correct defects, retain diary and registration number. Escalation: Do not compute filing deadline mechanically in unanswered-petition scenario (s22(1)(b)); seek JAG opinion.

title: Court-martial appellate assessment
body: AFT Act ss 15-17; Procedure Rules 4-10. Collect certified proceedings, findings, confirmation and petitions; Identify court-martial type, ranks, offences and sentences; Analyse s15 appellate jurisdiction separately from s3(o); Identify legal error, material irregularity and miscarriage; Check bail/suspension and statutory limitations; Prepare appeal relief and evidence-based record citations; Obtain legal vetting and file under current Bench practice. Escalation: SCM jurisdiction arguments require separate research; do not use blanket rejection.

title: Notice received by commanding officer
body: Procedure Rules 11,12,12A; AFT Act s23. Date-stamp summons and OA; Notify authorised legal chain and appoint case officer; Apply litigation hold to all relevant records; Create allegation-wise response matrix; Collect authenticated original documents and policy versions; Prepare factual comments, route through competent authority; Monitor filing date, hearing and any interim directions. Escalation: Never let an administrative counter reply contradict authenticated primary records.

title: Interim stay request and response
body: AFT Act s26; Procedure Rule 8(7)-(8). Verify imminent event and precise relief; Confirm service of interim papers or exceptional ex parte basis; Record present legal and factual position; Prepare focused response with documentary proof; On order receipt extract operative directions and effective time; Track s26(2) vacation process where applicable; Communicate stay or modification to implementing authority. Escalation: Section 26(2) contains conditional 14-day consequence; exact dates and court order control.

title: AFT case filing quality gate
body: Procedure Rules 4,5,8-12; 2011 Rule 12A. Verify party details and Bench; Check chronologically numbered facts; Identify precise legal grounds and prayers; Check statutory remedy and limitation narrative; Verify annexure citations against actual page numbers; Check affidavit, authority/vakalatnama and amended fees; Record filing, scrutiny and correction. Escalation: No legal filing should leave the unit with incomplete order or unsigned verification.

title: Review and correction after judgment
body: AFT Act s14(4)(f); Procedure Rule 18. Obtain signed order and record receipt date; Identify error apparent versus issue for appeal; Check 30-day review period; Apply authorised instructions for review decision; Prepare narrowly defined grounds and affidavit; Track Registry and Bench orders; Do not presume review stays original directions. Escalation: Review is not an unlimited rehearing.

title: Supreme Court statutory leave route
body: AFT Act ss 30-32. Classify final, interim or contempt order; Identify point of law of general public importance or SC leave issue; Record AFT decision date and 30-day leave deadline; If leave refused record refusal and second 30-day stage; Plan 90-day and other statutory clocks as applicable; Obtain government sanction or client instruction; Proceed with authorised counsel. Escalation: Sections 30,31 and 32 contain different time mechanisms; each must be separately analysed.

title: High Court review route
body: Constitution Art 226; Parashotam Dass 2023. Identify AFT stage and ordinary statutory alternative; Specify constitutional/jurisdictional error; Read Parashotam Dass and later territorial precedent; Assess self-restraint and alternative remedy concerns; Obtain precise forum opinion; Draft legally sustainable writ grounds; Track parallel appeal/review risk. Escalation: Do not describe Article 226 as an automatic factual appeal.

title: Implementation of AFT order
body: AFT Act ss 26,29. Obtain and authenticate full signed order; Extract operative paragraph, timing and conditions; Check stay or permitted review/appeal status; Assign to legally competent authority; Execute exact steps with documentary trail; Report compliance to legal chain and Tribunal if directed; Close only after verifying all monetary and service consequences. Escalation: Considering an appeal does not suspend an unstayed direction.

title: Pension claim litigation file
body: AFT Act ss 2,3(o),14,21-22; service pension rules. Collect status, PPO, Record Office and medical data; Identify entitlement regime applicable to retirement/casualty date; Reconcile claim, prior rejection and representation; Check continuing wrong and arrears issues separately; Obtain Accounts assessment and precise policy version; Draft clear cause and relief or para-wise response; Protect private medical/family records. Escalation: Do not calculate award from unofficial summary or a later pension circular alone.
references: AFT Act ss 2,3(o),14,21-22; service pension rules

title: Promotion/CR challenge file
body: AFT Act s3(o),s14; applicable policy. Identify exact selection cycle and rank cohort; Retrieve valid selection/CR policy on relevant date; Secure authorised record of assessment and communication; Check statutory complaint and final-order route; Analyse procedure, jurisdiction and bias allegations; Include third-party rights and confidentiality issues; Prepare legal response based on authentic record. Escalation: Avoid disclosing confidential selection details without proper authorisation.

title: Precedent update and version control
body: AFT Act, Constitution, Supreme Court/High Court/AFT rulings. Acquire judicial original and stable ID; Record legal question, holding and precise paragraph; Index later appeal, stay or overruling; Map geographic/binding status; Link case to each affected knowledge record; Have legal reviewer approve interpretation; Supersede stale digest with history intact. Escalation: The earlier 2015 writ-bar discussion must be linked to the 2023 Supreme Court ruling.
references: AFT Act, Constitution, Supreme Court/High Court/AFT rulings

title: Officer loses promotion selection
body: Perspective: Applicant. Officer receives non-selection communication, statutory complaint rejected, seeks AFT remedy. Recommended assessment: Check service-matter jurisdiction and relief, obtain applicable policy/board records, check s21 and s22, avoid asking court to simply replace board merits.

title: Pension arrears for 17 years
body: Perspective: Applicant. Retired JCO discovers alleged pension underpayment dating back 17 years. Recommended assessment: Separate recurring present underpayment from historic arrears; compare Tarsem Singh, old PPO, refusals and statutory limitation. No promise of entire arrears.

title: CO served with OA and stay request
body: Perspective: Respondent. Unit gets AFT papers asking for an interim stay within 48 hours. Recommended assessment: Stamp time, notify legal cell, hold records, identify operative status and respond; on any stay, notify action officer immediately.

title: No response to statutory complaint
body: Perspective: Applicant. An officer sent a competent statutory complaint; no reply for eight months. Recommended assessment: Six-month deemed exhaustion under s21(2)(b) can be assessed; s22(b) filing time must be legally reviewed; retain proof of receipt.

title: Thirty-day SCM detention challenged
body: Perspective: Appeal. Soldier challenges an SCM sentence of 30 days detention and asks if AFT has jurisdiction. Recommended assessment: Separate s3(o) service-matter exclusion from s15 appellate power and research Nk Santosh Lohar/subsequent treatment.

title: Court-martial conviction after witness refusal
body: Perspective: Appeal. Accused argues key defence witness was wrongly refused during SCM/GCM. Recommended assessment: Locate trial order and relevance, assess s15(4) legal error and miscarriage, examine complete proceedings and confirmation.

title: OA filed in wrong Bench
body: Perspective: Registry. Retiree originally served in North India but now ordinarily resides elsewhere. Recommended assessment: Check Rule 6(2) retired resident option, cause-of-action and roster; seek registry clarification if territorial conflict.

title: Registry defect after filing
body: Perspective: Registry. AFT returns application for missing annexures. Recommended assessment: Preserve acknowledgement and defect memo; correct within authorised interval; track Rule5 registration and challenge route.

title: Copy of AFT decision received today
body: Perspective: Applicant. Unsuccessful applicant asks whether to seek review or Supreme Court leave. Recommended assessment: Capture decision and service dates; compare Rule18 30-day review and ss30-31 leave rules; do not treat as interchangeable.

title: AFT order remands promotion decision
body: Perspective: Unit. Tribunal directs competent authority to reconsider rather than award a promotion. Recommended assessment: Read operative paragraph, route to authorised board/authority, document reconsideration, not grant direct rank by CO.

title: Pending appeal but no stay
body: Perspective: Unit. Government considers Supreme Court appeal against pension direction; order remains unstayed. Recommended assessment: Seek competent implementation decision, obtain legal advice, do not assume merely filing appeal suspends order.

title: Classified report sought in proceedings
body: Perspective: Unit. Applicant seeks a classified operation-related record. Recommended assessment: Preserve record, consult competent security/privilege authority and government counsel, consider protected production/in-camera procedure.

title: Widow contests family pension refusal
body: Perspective: Applicant. Widow seeks a pension claim based on deceased soldier service. Recommended assessment: Check s2(2), claimant status, nomination/heirs, pension policy on relevant date, claim communications and AFT jurisdiction.

title: Fresh reminder about old rejection
body: Perspective: Applicant. An officer sends repeated representations about 2017 discharge denial. Recommended assessment: Assess first operative order, new policy/independent decision if any, and delay; avoid resetting clock by routine reminder.

title: Court issues ex parte interim order
body: Perspective: Unit. AFT stay was granted without respondent being heard and unit wants vacation. Recommended assessment: Read s26(2) exact conditions and 14-day consequence; record date of receipt, copy service, written vacation application and notice.

title: Third-party promotion impact
body: Perspective: Applicant/Respondent. Proposed seniority correction would adversely affect another serving officer. Recommended assessment: Identify necessary parties and settled rights; distinguish continuing wrong; provide hearing and current seniority policy.

title: Government affidavit with no eyewitness
body: Perspective: Respondent. Records Officer must verify a decades-old accident narrative. Recommended assessment: Differentiate record-derived knowledge from eyewitness evidence, identify source document for each paragraph, attach lawful authorisation.

title: High Court petition against AFT
body: Perspective: Higher courts. Party seeks Article 226 review after AFT order with alleged jurisdictional error. Recommended assessment: Apply Parashotam Dass alongside specialist-forum and self-restraint principles; distinguish statutory leave and constitutional review.

title: AFT jurisdiction screen
body: Before suggesting AFT route. Service status verified; Remedy classification s14 versus s15; s3(o) inclusions/exclusions recorded; Territorial Bench checked; Any SCM ambiguity flagged; Legal route approved

title: Statutory complaint and limitation
body: Before OA filing. Competent representation proof; Final rejection or non-disposal date; Six-month exhaustion checked; s22 limitation analysis signed; Need for condonation examined; All chronology dates supported

title: Original Application packet
body: Before Registry submission. Form and proper case type; List of dates and index; Numbered paragraphs and relief; Impugned order annexed; Every relied document paginated; Affidavit and vakalatnama where needed; Fee category checked against 2011 amendment; Receipt and defect follow-up recorded

title: Unit receives Tribunal notice
body: Within authorised direction deadlines. Receipt time stamped; Legal cell informed; Record preservation issued; Responsible case officer nominated; Full OA and attachments distributed securely; Para-wise matrix and evidence prepared; Filing and hearing dates tracked

title: Government counter-affidavit
body: Before signing. Every allegation admitted/denied/explained; Source document for each disputed fact; Correct policy version and authorised signer; Affidavit reflects actual source of knowledge; No records suppressed; Sensitive material properly handled; Respondent approval chain complete

title: Interim relief/stay
body: When stay sought or received. Application and documents served or exception reasoned; Urgency and irreparable consequences addressed; Exact interim prayer identified; Operative direction and start date recorded; Competent implementing authority notified; Vacation timelines checked under s26; Certified copy preserved

title: Court-martial appeal
body: Before lodging appeal. Court type, charges, rank and punishment captured; Certified trial record; Confirmation/promulgation available; Statutory petition trail; Each error tied to trial page; Miscarriage/legality analysis; Sentence mitigation grounds separated; SCM route review signed

title: Post-judgment remedies
body: After adverse AFT judgment. Certified order and receipt date; Operative directions extracted; Review Rule18 timing assessed; Leave s31 30+30 day stages tracked; s30 statutory periods checked; Government or client sanction documented; Stay status and implementation tracked

title: Order execution and closeout
body: Before closing litigation. Exact operative clauses implemented; Approved authority signed action; Financial or service records corrected; Proof sent through counsel; Any appeal/stay status recorded; No outstanding deadline; Records archived under litigation hold policy

title: Precedent verification
body: Before citing a case. Original judgment retrieved; Judicial level and territorial reach recorded; Precise relevant paragraph checked; Later appeal/stay/review searched; Distinguish ratio and obiter; Effective policy and fact pattern matched; JAG review signoff

title: L. Chandra Kumar v Union of India
body: Supreme Court 18 March 1997 (1997) 3 SCC 261 Constitutional judicial review of tribunal decisions High Courts’ supervisory constitutional judicial-review role is part of the constitutional framework; tribunals are supplemental specialist fora, not total constitutional replacements. Do not bypass first-instance specialist forum for routine service grievances; distinguish AFT-specific law.

title: Union of India v Major General Shri Kant Sharma
body: Supreme Court 11 March 2015 (2015) 6 SCC 773 Historical restrictive view of AFT writ review Earlier decision reasoned toward restriction on High Court review given statutory appellate scheme. Must never be served as unqualified current rule; subsequent Supreme Court Parashotam Dass (2023) clarified Article 226 cannot be barred.

title: Union of India v Parashotam Dass
body: Supreme Court 21 March 2023 2023 INSC 265; Civil Appeal No 447 of 2023 Article 226 High Court review of AFT orders Complete exclusion of Article 226 judicial review of AFT decisions cannot stand; Court distinguished Art 226 judicial review from Art 227 superintendence. A writ is not routine second appeal; High Court self-restraint and first-instance doctrine remain relevant; show both this case and 2026 Delhi HC.

title: Union of India v Tarsem Singh
body: Supreme Court 13 August 2008 (2008) 8 SCC 648 Continuing wrong, limitation, arrears, third-party rights Continuing service wrong may remain capable of correction; arrears are not necessarily unlimited, and delay exceptions do not ordinarily upset settled third-party rights such as promotion/seniority. Read with AFT Act s22; this decision does not independently extend every pension limitation period.

title: Nk Santosh Lohar v Union of India
body: Punjab & Haryana High Court 4 October 2023 2023:PHHC:127834 SCM and AFT statutory appeal classification Examined interface of s3(o)(iv) and s15; reasoned that SCM orders may reach tribunal by appellate pathway independently of service-matter wording. High Court decision is jurisdiction-sensitive; check binding precedents and any later overruling or Supreme Court treatment.

title: Lt Col Pandappa Kotagi v Union of India
body: Delhi High Court 5 May 2026 W.P.(C) 5992/2026 First-instance AFT service disputes under Art 226 framework Court discussed why a servicematter ordinarily belongs in AFT despite availability of constitutional judicial review in appropriate cases. Do not use Art 226 as routine method of bypassing AFT; use updated High Court/SC treatment.

title: S.N. Mukherjee v Union of India
body: Supreme Court 1990 (1990) 4 SCC 594 Reasoned decisions and military proceedings Major judgment on reason-giving and constitutional review concerning military decision-making; exact holdings require review of original paragraphs for the particular proposition invoked. Original judgment and controlling proposition must be paragraph-verified before operational use; marked review pending.
